title: Authority: MCP server (vtt-mcp)
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §5.1, §5.2 (Query, Write, Explain, Subscribe; "anything a human can do through the UI must be expressible through this surface"; limits), §5.3; docs/PROTOCOL.md §11 (MCP tools, resources, change polling) as written by vtt-5su.2.

Exclusive files: `packages/authority/src/mcp/server.ts`, `tools.ts`, `changes.ts`, `resources.ts`, `src/bin/mcp.ts`, tests `test/mcp/*.test.ts`; the sorted line `export * from "./mcp/server"` in `packages/authority/src/index.ts`. Adds `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.3.1 (dependency) and `@modelcontextprotocol/client` 2.3.1 (devDependency) to `@vtt/authority`, and `"vtt-mcp": "./src/bin/mcp.ts"` to its `bin`. The SDK's exact API (server class, tool and resource registration, stdio server transport, an in-process transport pair for tests, stdio client transport) is taken from the installed packages' type declarations. If 2.3.1 lacks a stdio server transport or zod-4 tool input schemas, stop and report; do not switch SDKs.

`createMcpServer({client: ProtocolClient, name = "vtt"})` registers these tools; input schemas are vtt-5su.3's params schemas, results are vtt-5su.3's result objects returned as `structuredContent` plus one JSON text block:

| Tool | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| table_info | `{revision, boards, table, limits, actor}` from the client |
| list_objects, get_objects, evaluate, zones, at_position, changes_since, log | the same-named methods |
| explain_cell, explain_group, explain_action | the same-named methods |
| transact | `transact` with `base_revision` required; `txn_id` generated when absent; on `disconnected` waits up to 10 s for reconnection and resends once with the same `txn_id` |
| undo | `undo` (targets `latest`, `mine`, `group`; `expect_index`) |
| save | `save` |
| subscribe | `subscribe` (scopes `board`, `objects`, `all`; GM viewer) plus a `ChangeBuffer`; returns `{subscription, revision, objects: <count>}` |
| poll_changes | `{subscription, wait_ms? (0..30000, default 0)}`: returns and clears the buffered changes, waiting up to `wait_ms` for the first |
| unsubscribe | `unsubscribe`, drops the buffer |

- `ChangeBuffer` (changes.ts): per commit, from the mirror before and after the delta, `{revision, group: GroupHeader, created: ObjectId[], removed: ObjectId[], cells: {object, cell, before?: CellView, after?: CellView}[]}`; keeps at most 1,000 commits, then drops the oldest and sets `overflowed: true` in the next `poll_changes` result (the agent then uses `changes_since`). After a `resync` it records `{resync: true, from_revision, to_revision}`. Each buffered commit also sends `notifications/resources/updated` for `vtt://subscriptions/<id>`; reading that resource returns the buffer without clearing it.
- Results: a `ProtocolError` → `isError: true` with `{code, message}`; `status: "rejected"` → `isError: true` with the rejection and `op_index`; committed and query results → normal.
- Resources (resources.ts): `vtt://docs/formulas`, `vtt://docs/design`, `vtt://docs/protocol` (docs/FORMULAS.md, DESIGN.md, PROTOCOL.md read at runtime via `new URL("../../../../docs/…", import.meta.url)`), and `vtt://schema/ops` (JSON Schema of `WireOp`, all 19 kinds, from zod's `z.toJSONSchema`).
- Tool descriptions say: ids should be human-meaningful (DESIGN §5.3); writes need the latest `revision` (from `table_info`, a result, or `poll_changes`); one `transact` is one undoable group; formulas and actions follow docs/FORMULAS.md (resource).
- `bin/mcp.ts` (shebang `#!/usr/bin/env -S node --import tsx`): `vtt-mcp [--url u] [--token t] [--name n]`, else env `VTT_URL`/`VTT_TOKEN`, else `readSessionFile()` (vtt-5su.10); connects a `ProtocolClient` with `kind: "agent"` and `agent_name` = `--name` or the MCP client's `clientInfo.name`; serves MCP over stdio; writes logs only to stderr. While the authority is unreachable, tools return `isError` with `{code:"disconnected"}` and the client keeps reconnecting.

Done when: tests start `TableHost.inMemory` + `startServer` on port 0 and connect an MCP client to `createMcpServer` through the SDK's in-process transport: the tool list equals the table (names and required arguments, frozen as a snapshot in the test); a parity test asserts every protocol method except `invoke` and `document` has a tool and that every one of the 19 `WireOp` kinds validates in the `transact` tool's input schema; one happy path and one error per tool; a stale `transact` returns `isError` with `stale_write`; after `subscribe`, a GM write through a second `ProtocolClient` releases a pending `poll_changes` (`wait_ms: 2000`) with a cell change carrying `before`, `after` and actor `gm`; 1,001 commits set `overflowed`; reading `vtt://docs/formulas` returns text starting with "# Formula and Action Language"; `vtt://schema/ops` lists 19 op kinds; a socket dropped during `transact` is retried once with the same `txn_id` and exactly one group is committed; spawning `vtt-mcp --url … --token …` as a subprocess and connecting the SDK's stdio client transport lists the tools; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: the `invoke` tool (M5); a built-in agent (Later); MCP over HTTP (Later); prompts; character-viewer subscriptions for agents (GM only in v1).

Depends on: vtt-5su.10, vtt-5su.7.

title: Authority: WebSocket server and vtt-serve
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 Platform ("a local process … serves the UI over localhost with the op stream over a WebSocket"), §5.2 ("trusts its single connection … Query and write limits exist so a runaway agent cannot stall the table"); docs/PROTOCOL.md §1 (transport, envelope, close codes), §2 (hello, auth, origin, discovery), §3 (actors), §8 (ordering, heartbeat), §10 (errors, limits) as written by vtt-5su.2.

Exclusive files: `packages/authority/src/server/server.ts`, `connection.ts`, `router.ts`, `session-file.ts`, `src/bin/serve.ts`, tests `test/server/*.test.ts`; sorted lines `export * from "./server/server"` and `"./server/session-file"` in `packages/authority/src/index.ts`. Adds to `@vtt/authority`'s package.json: dependencies `ws` 8.22.0 and `tsx` 4.23.15, devDependency `@types/ws` 8.18.2, `"bin": {"vtt-serve": "./src/bin/serve.ts"}`; root package.json script `"serve": "node --import tsx packages/authority/src/bin/serve.ts"`. `serve.ts` starts with `#!/usr/bin/env -S node --import tsx`.

- `startServer({host: TableHost, port = DEFAULT_PORT, hostname = "127.0.0.1", token?, allowOrigins = [], helloTimeoutMs = 5000}): Promise<{url, port, token, close(): Promise<void>}>`; `port: 0` picks a free port; `url` is `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/ws`; the token is the given one or 32 random bytes base64url. Node `http` server: `GET /healthz` → `200 {"ok":true,"revision":n}`; every other path 404; WebSocket upgrades (ws `noServer`, `maxPayload = max_message_bytes`) only on `/ws`. An upgrade whose `Origin` header is present and is neither `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, `http://localhost:<port>` nor in `allowOrigins` is refused with HTTP 403 before upgrading.
- Connection (`connection.ts`): `awaiting_hello` → `ready`. No `hello` within `helloTimeoutMs` → close 4408. The first message must be `hello`; any other first message, or a wrong token (constant-time comparison), → `goodbye` + close 4401; a `protocol` other than 1 → `goodbye` + close 4400. Actor: `client.kind: "agent"` → `{type:"agent", name: agent_name ?? client.name}`; otherwise `{type:"gm"}`. Reply `welcome` with session id, actor, revision, boards, table `{name: basename, path}`, `LIMITS`; register the connection with the `SubscriptionHub` (vtt-5su.9).
- Requests: parsed with `parseClientMessage`; a parse failure answers `bad_request` (with the id when it could be read, else null) and keeps the connection. A token bucket of `max_requests_per_second` per connection; an excess request answers `busy`. A connection whose `bufferedAmount` exceeds `max_buffered_bytes` is closed 4429. `router.ts` maps methods: `transact`, `undo` → vtt-5su.5 (`CommandContext` with the connection's actor and kind, the host's dice, one server-wide `TxnCache`); queries and explain → vtt-5su.8; `subscribe`, `unsubscribe` → vtt-5su.9; `save` → `host.save()`; `invoke` → `unsupported`. `ProtocolFailure` → its error; any other exception → `internal` (logged to stderr with the request id), the connection stays open.
- Ordering: messages are handled one at a time in arrival order across connections (handlers are synchronous); commit events from `hub.onCommitEvent` are sent as they are produced, so every connection receives them in revision order and the committing connection receives the commit event before its response.
- Heartbeat: ws ping every 15 s; a connection missing two pongs is terminated. `host.onSave` results are broadcast as `save` events to every ready connection. On close: `hub.dropConnection`.
- `session-file.ts`: `sessionFilePath()` = `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/vtt/session.json` (default `~/.config/vtt/session.json`); `writeSessionFile({url, token, pid, table})` (directory 0700, file 0600); `readSessionFile(): SessionInfo | null`; `removeSessionFile(pid)` removes the file only when its pid matches.
- `bin/serve.ts`: `vtt-serve <file> [--port n] [--token t] [--allow-origin o]… [--no-autosave] [--print-session]` (`--token` fixes the token, e.g. across restarts in tests): `TableHost.open(file, {createIfMissing: true, autosave})`, `startServer`, `writeSessionFile`; `--print-session` prints one JSON line `{"url":…,"token":…}` to stdout once listening. SIGINT/SIGTERM: stop accepting, send `goodbye` and close connections with 1001, `host.close()` (final save), remove the session file, exit 0. Exit 1 with a one-line message when the table is locked or the port is in use.

Done when: tests with a real server on port 0 and Node's global `WebSocket` show: `/healthz` answers with the revision; a wrong token, a wrong protocol, a non-hello first message and a missing hello (`helloTimeoutMs: 100`) each close with their code; a foreign `Origin` gets 403 and an `allowOrigins` entry connects; `welcome` carries `{type:"gm"}` for `ui` and `{type:"agent", name}` for `agent`; a malformed request gets `bad_request` and the next request works; an oversize frame closes the connection; 300 requests in one burst get some `busy`; two clients: A subscribes to a board, B commits a `transact`, A receives the commit event with a delta, B receives its commit event before its response; ten interleaved transacts from two clients give strictly increasing revisions seen in the same order by both; a handler that throws answers `internal` and the connection survives; `invoke` answers `unsupported`; `save` writes the file and broadcasts a `save` event; spawning `vtt-serve` as a subprocess on a temp file with `--print-session` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` in a temp directory writes the session file with mode 0600, serves `/healthz`, and on SIGTERM saves, removes the session file and exits 0; a second `vtt-serve` on the same file exits 1; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: serving the UI's static files, token injection into the page, and assets (M4); TLS and remote access (Later); the client (vtt-5su.7); MCP (vtt-5su.11); multiplayer rights (Later).

Depends on: vtt-5su.3, vtt-5su.5, vtt-5su.8, vtt-5su.9, vtt-5su.4.

title: Authority: subscriptions and commit deltas
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §7 ("Propagation is lazy pull with dirty marking … The authority decides which cells to recompute and send", with vtt-5su.2's added sentence); DESIGN.md §5.2 Subscribe, §7 (internal synchronization before public notifications), §4.4; docs/PROTOCOL.md §8 (subscriptions, commit events, ordering) as written by vtt-5su.2.

Exclusive files: `packages/authority/src/protocol/subscriptions.ts`, `test/protocol/subscriptions*.test.ts`; the sorted line `export * from "./protocol/subscriptions"` in `packages/authority/src/index.ts`; one addition to `src/engine/table.ts` (vtt-75c.12): `table.onCommit(fn): () => void` whose payload is `{group, summary, dirty: CellKey[]}` (`dirty` = the keys `engine.invalidate` returned), called after the internal hook has updated the index and invalidated the engine, so listeners never read stale values.

`new SubscriptionHub(table)`:

- `subscribe(conn: string, params: SubscribeParams): SubscribeResult`: at most `max_subscriptions` per connection (`ProtocolFailure("busy")`); subscription ids are `"s"` + a hub-wide counter. Scope at the current revision: `board` = every object directly on the board and, recursively, everything in their contents; `objects` = the ids (with `subtree`, also their descendants; ids that do not exist are ignored); `all` = every live object; `log` = no objects. Builds every view with vtt-5su.6 (viewer and `cells` from params), stores per subscription `last: Map<ObjectId, string>` (canonical JSON of each sent view) and the sent cover keys, and returns `{subscription, revision, objects, covers}` (covers for every board in scope; for `log`, `groups` = the newest 50 group views, objects and covers empty).
- `onCommitEvent(fn: (conn: string, event: CommitEvent) => void)`: on each `table.onCommit`, for every connection known to the hub (registered by `addConnection(conn)`, also implicitly by `subscribe`), one `CommitEvent`: `revision`, `group` header, `boards` (all boards) when the summary created, removed or renamed a board, and `deltas` for that connection's subscriptions that changed; a connection without changes gets `deltas: []`.
- Delta algorithm. Candidates = objects of `summary.created`, `removed`, `moved` (plus both containers of every move), `writtenCells`, `visibility`, `actionsChanged`, and the objects of `dirty` keys. GM subscription: re-view the candidates plus objects that entered or left scope. Character subscription: re-view the whole scope when the commit is visibility-relevant (any changed or dirty key whose cell is `visible_to`, `face_up`, `opaque`, `owner`, `is_zone`, `position`, `rotation`, `shape`, `board`, `container` or `contents`; any `cell_visibility` effect; any create or remove), else only the candidates. Building a view pulls its formula cells; dirty cells outside every scope stay dirty. A view whose canonical JSON differs from `last` goes into `objects`; an object that left scope, was removed, or became invisible goes into `removed`; covers are diffed by key for every board in scope. A `log` subscription receives the new group's view and, for an undo group, the undone group's view again (now `undone: true`).
- `unsubscribe(conn, id)` (unknown id: `not_found`), `dropConnection(conn)` free state; `stats(): {viewsBuilt}` for tests.

Done when: (1) equivalence property test: for seeded random sequences of 200 commits over a 60-object table (writes, formula sets, overrides, moves between boards and containers, spawns, removes, `visible_to` changes on containers, opaque zone toggles and moves, face flips, per-cell visibility, undo), for the GM and Aldric and for `board`, `objects` (subtree) and `all` scopes, applying each delta to the previous state equals a fresh `subscribe` at every revision (objects and covers); (2) a die moved into the dice tray yields a delta containing the tray with its new sum although the die was never its dependency; (3) revealing a room zone to Aldric yields cover removal and upserts of the tokens under it for Aldric's subscription and only the zone's view for the GM's; (4) on a 3,000-object board a write to a literal cell with no dependents builds at most 3 views for a GM subscription (`stats`); (5) a formula cell outside every scope is not evaluated by the commit (engine `stats().evaluations` unchanged) while a subscribed dependent is recomputed; (6) inside the commit listener `table.value` already reflects the commit; (7) a connection with no subscriptions receives `deltas: []`; (8) the 17th subscription is `busy`; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: transport and wire ordering (vtt-5su.10); MCP change buffers (vtt-5su.11); finer index dependency keys (Polish); cell-level patches (Polish).

Depends on: vtt-5su.6, vtt-75c.12.

title: Authority: queries and explain
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §5.2 Query and Explain (list objects paged, read cells, resolve formulas, enumerate zones and their contents, what is at a position, what changed since revision N; "the formula, dependency chain, and action steps behind any value or log entry"), §4.4; FORMULAS.md §5 (query order), §7 (dynamic dependencies), §9; docs/PROTOCOL.md §4 (methods), §9 (explain, evaluate, at_position, document) as written by vtt-5su.2.

Exclusive files: `packages/authority/src/protocol/queries.ts`, `explain.ts`, tests `test/protocol/queries.test.ts`, `explain.test.ts`; sorted lines `export * from "./protocol/explain"` and `export * from "./protocol/queries"` in `packages/authority/src/index.ts`. Every function takes `(table, params)` and returns the vtt-5su.3 result type; failures throw `ProtocolFailure(code, message)`. Views and group views come from vtt-5su.6's `ViewBuilder`.

- `listObjects`: candidates are all live objects, filtered by every given `filter` field (`board`: directly on it; `container`: directly in it; `tag`: its tag list contains the text; `name`: literal name equal; flags equal), then by `canSeeObject` for the viewer; ordered by id (code point); `cursor` is the last id of the previous page (results start after it); `limit` defaults to 50; `next_cursor` is null on the last page. Pages may span revisions; each page reports its revision.
- `getObjects`: views in request order; ids that do not exist or are invisible to the viewer go to `missing`, indistinguishably.
- `evaluateAdhoc` (GM only; no viewer parameter): `engine.evaluate(source, {thisId})` (vtt-o9i.16); `source.length` ≤ `max_source_length` else `bad_request`; an unknown `this` is `not_found`; without `this`, `this` evaluates as for a formula with no object (the engine's ad hoc default); results pass through unredacted.
- `zonesOnBoard`: every `is_zone` object directly on the board and visible to the viewer, ordered by id; `contents` = `engine.evaluate("contents(this)", {thisId: zone})` (FORMULAS §5 order), restricted to objects the viewer can see; `view` = structural view.
- `atPosition`: candidates `index.candidates(board, pointBounds)` (vtt-75c.9) where `pointBounds` is the degenerate box at the point; `objects` = non-zone candidates whose evaluated footprint contains the point by vtt-75c.7's `pointInRegion` (boundary inclusive; a shapeless object matches when its anchor is within `GEOM_EPSILON`), ordered ascending `z` (empty = 0) then id; `zones` = zone candidates containing the point, same order; both filtered by `canSeeObject`; objects in containers are never included.
- `changesSince`: retained groups with `revision > params.revision`, oldest first, at most `limit`, `more` when cut; `truncated` when `params.revision` is below the oldest retained group's `base_revision`; each through `groupView(…, {effects: true})`, nulls dropped.
- `logPage`: retained groups newest first, `before` an exclusive absolute index, `effects` per the parameter; `first_index`, `next_index`, `undo_barrier` from `History` (vtt-75c.5).
- `documentDump` (GM only): `store.toSnapshot()` plus the retained log `{first_index, groups, undo_barrier}`.
- `explainCell`: `table.value` first (forcing evaluation), then `engine.dependenciesOf` (vtt-o9i.9); dependencies expanded breadth first to `depth`, each cell expanded once, at most `max_explain_nodes` nodes (`truncated` when cut). `content` reports `parses` (and `syntax_error` when it does not) for formula cells. For a character viewer: a cell it cannot see appears as `{type:"cell", object, cell, hidden: true}` without value; a dependency on an object it cannot see has `object: null` and no value; `source` omitted; values redacted. `error_chain` follows the `origin` of the cell's error to the next cell's error until a cell whose error's origin is itself (or a repeat), at most 32 steps, redacted the same way. `last_write` is the newest retained group with a `cell` effect on that cell (header plus the effect's `cause`). An unknown object or cell is `not_found`.
- `explainGroup`: `{group: groupView(…, {effects: true}), action?}`; `action` is the origin action's current definition when its object still exists and the viewer is the GM, with `current: true`. An index not retained (or a group invisible to the viewer) is `not_found`.
- `explainAction`: `when` evaluated by `engine.evaluate(when, {thisId})`; `enabled` iff `when` is absent or evaluates to `true`; `reason` `when_false` (false or another non-error value) or `when_error`; `source` and `steps` GM only. An unknown action is `not_found`.

Done when: tests show: paging 120 objects with `limit: 50` gives three pages, no duplicates, ascending ids; a `tag: "creature"` filter over fireball.json's setup returns its creatures; Aldric's `list_objects` excludes a GM-only object and `get_objects` lists it in `missing` exactly like a removed id; `evaluate("max_hp - damage_taken", this goblin1)` gives 27, then 22 after a write; a 10,001-character source is `bad_request`; `zones` on difficult-terrain.json's board lists the zone with the token after a move in and without it after the move out; `at_position` inside two stacked tokens returns both in ascending `z`, and inside a rotated rect zone returns the zone; `changes_since(r)` after three commits returns three groups oldest first, and after `compactLog` a too-old `r` is `truncated`; `explain_cell` of `hp` at depth 1 lists `max_hp` and `damage_taken` with values, and at depth 2 over a three-cell chain shows the nested node; the dice-tray sum lists an `index` dependency; Aldric's `explain_cell` of `hit` names `goblin1.ac` with `hidden: true` and no value; a `#REF` cell's `error_chain` ends at the cell that read the deleted object; a `#CYCLE` chain terminates; `last_write` names the group that last wrote the cell; an unparsable formula reports `parses: false`; `explain_action` on attack-card.json's card reports `Roll` disabled with `when_false` while `target` is empty and enabled after it is set; `explain_group` of a committed `setTag` group returns its field effect; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: subscriptions (vtt-5su.9); transport (vtt-5su.10); log sentences (M5); action step parsing (M5); viewer-specific evaluate (GM only by decision).

Depends on: vtt-5su.6, vtt-75c.7, vtt-75c.12.

title: Protocol: client and view mirror
description:
Implements: docs/PROTOCOL.md §1–§3 (transport, hello, actors), §8 (commit events, ordering, reconnection) as written by vtt-5su.2; DESIGN.md §7 ("The UI and the agent are two clients of the same protocol").

Exclusive files: `packages/protocol/src/client.ts`, `mirror.ts`, tests `test/client*.test.ts`, `test/mirror.test.ts`, `test/support/fake-server.ts`; sorted lines `export * from "./client"` and `export * from "./mirror"` in `packages/protocol/src/index.ts`. Browser-safe: neither file imports `node:` modules (a test reads both sources and asserts it).

- `new ProtocolClient({url, token, client: {name, kind}, agent_name?, WebSocket = globalThis.WebSocket, reconnect = {initialMs: 250, maxMs: 5000, factor: 2} | false, requestTimeoutMs = 30000})`.
- `connect(): Promise<Welcome>` (sends `hello` first; rejects on `goodbye`); `state`: `"connecting" | "open" | "reconnecting" | "closed"`; `revision` (from `welcome`, then from every commit event); `actor`; `limits`; `boards` (from `welcome` and commit events carrying `boards`); `close()`.
- `request<M>(method, params): Promise<Result<M>>`: request ids are a per-client counter rendered as strings; rejects with the `ProtocolError` of an error response, with `{code:"timeout"}` after `requestTimeoutMs`, and every pending request with `{code:"disconnected"}` when the socket drops. Every incoming message is validated with `parseServerMessage`; an invalid one closes the socket (then reconnects).
- `transact(ops, {label?, base_revision = this.revision, txn_id = crypto.randomUUID(), actor?})`: convenience over `request("transact", …)`; never retries by itself.
- `subscribe(params): Promise<Subscription>`; `Subscription = {id, params, mirror: ViewMirror, on(event: "delta" | "resync", fn), close(): Promise<void>}` (close sends `unsubscribe`).
- `ViewMirror` (mirror.ts): `objects: Map<ObjectId, ObjectView>`, `covers: Map<string, Cover>`, `groups: GroupView[]` (log scope, newest first; a group view with an existing index replaces it), `revision`; `reset(initial: SubscribeResult)`; `apply(delta: SubscriptionDelta, revision)` upserts objects, deletes `removed`, applies cover upserts and removals, merges groups.
- `on("commit" | "save" | "state", fn)`.
- Reconnection: on an unexpected close (not `close()`, not 4400 or 4401) reconnect with exponential backoff (`initialMs`, ×`factor`, capped at `maxMs`); after the new `welcome`, resubscribe every live subscription with its original params (the subscription id may change; the `Subscription` object stays), `reset` its mirror from the new result, and emit `resync {from_revision, to_revision}`. 4400 and 4401 are terminal (`closed`).

Done when: tests against `fake-server.ts` (an in-memory WebSocket-shaped peer scripted per test, injected through the `WebSocket` option) show: `hello` is the first frame and carries the token; request/response correlation with responses out of order; error responses reject with the error; timeout and disconnect rejections; `revision` follows commit events; a mirror fed an initial view and three deltas equals the expected maps, including an object removal and a cover removal; after a dropped socket the client reconnects at 250, 500, 1000 ms (fake timers), resubscribes with the same params, resets mirrors and emits `resync`; 4401 is terminal; `transact` fills `base_revision` and a UUID `txn_id`; the two source files contain no `node:` import; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: the server (vtt-5su.10); MCP (vtt-5su.11); UI state management (M4); automatic write retries (vtt-5su.11 decides for MCP); integration with the real server (vtt-5su.11, vtt-5su.12).

Depends on: vtt-5su.3.

title: Authority: viewer-filtered views
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.4 (effective visibility, per-cell visibility, face-down rule, opaque cover, "the log, and the agent's query results are all filtered by the same effective visibility", fail closed), §7 ("clients receive cell results, never inputs"); FORMULAS.md §9; docs/PROTOCOL.md §7 (views, redaction, covers, face-down exemptions, log filtering) as written by vtt-5su.2.

Exclusive files: `packages/authority/src/protocol/views.ts`, `test/protocol/views.test.ts`; one sorted line `export * from "./protocol/views"` in `packages/authority/src/index.ts`. Consumes vtt-75c.10's `Visibility` and `FACE_DOWN_EXEMPT` unchanged (no edit to visibility.ts).

`new ViewBuilder(table, viewer)`: one instance per build pass at one revision; memoizes `canSeeObject` and `canSeeCell` per (object, cell) within the pass. `STRUCTURAL_VIEW_CELLS` = every readable structural cell of `STRUCTURAL_CELLS` (vtt-75c.3) except `id`.

- `objectView(id, cells: "all" | "structural" | string[]): ObjectView | null`. GM: never null for a live object; `cells` holds every stored user cell plus every `STRUCTURAL_VIEW_CELLS` cell (defaults included), each `{value: table.value(id, cell), kind, source?, overridden?, visibility?}` with `source` for formula cells, `overridden` for formula cells, `visibility` when the object has a `cell_visibility` entry for it; `actions` with `when` and `steps`. Character viewer: null unless `canSeeObject`; a cell appears iff `canSeeCell`; no `source`, no `visibility`; `actions` carry names only. `"structural"` restricts to `STRUCTURAL_VIEW_CELLS`; a list restricts to those names (absent names are missing).
- Redaction, character viewers only: every ref, top level, in a list (recursively) or as a viewers entry, naming an object the viewer cannot see becomes `{type:"redacted"}` in place; an error value whose `origin` names an object the viewer cannot see or a cell it cannot see becomes `{type:"error", code}` only.
- `covers(board): Cover[]`, character viewers only (GM: `[]`): for each zone on the board that vtt-75c.12's cover query reports as covering or undetermined and that the viewer cannot effectively see, one `Cover` with the zone's evaluated `position`, `rotation` (empty → 0) and `shape`, or `{whole_board: true}` when undetermined. `key` is stable per zone for the life of the process and does not contain the zone id (`"c"` + a counter assigned on first use, kept in a map owned by the `Table`'s lifetime, e.g. a `WeakMap<Table, Map<ObjectId, string>>`).
- `groupView(group, {effects: boolean}): GroupView | null`. GM: the group's fields plus `undone` from `History.isUndone`, with `effects` when asked. Character viewer, by current visibility: `names` restricted to objects the viewer can see now; with `effects`, only effects whose objects are all visible now and, for `cell` and `cell_visibility` effects, whose cell the viewer can see; `before`/`after` values redacted as above; effects on removed objects dropped. A group with no remaining names and no remaining effects is null (omitted); otherwise its header (index, revision, actor, kind, label) is kept.

title: Authority: command execution (transact, undo, stale writes)
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §5.2 Write ("validated commands … carry the revision they were based on, and are rejected on conflict"), §7 (transactions, one group per command, undo targets); docs/PROTOCOL.md §3 (actors), §5 (ops, bindings), §6 (revisions, stale writes, retries) as written by vtt-5su.2.

The transport-free command layer. Exclusive files: `packages/authority/src/protocol/commands.ts`, `conflicts.ts`, tests `test/protocol/commands.test.ts`, `conflicts.test.ts`. Adds the sorted lines `export * from "./protocol/commands"` and `export * from "./protocol/conflicts"` to `packages/authority/src/index.ts` (no `protocol/index.ts`; every M3 module is exported from the package index directly). Two permitted edits to M2 files: if vtt-75c.16's `Transaction` has no list of recorded effects, add a read-only `tx.effects(): readonly Effect[]` to `store/transaction.ts` (one method, nothing else); if vtt-75c.8 does not export its key-intersection helper, export it from `store/undo.ts` as `keysIntersect(a: string[], b: string[]): string[]` (returning the intersecting keys) instead of reimplementing the rule.

```ts
type CommandContext = { table: Table; actor: Actor; kind: "ui" | "agent" | "test"; dice: DiceSource; txns: TxnCache };
executeTransact(ctx: CommandContext, params: TransactParams): TransactResult;
executeUndo(ctx: CommandContext, params: UndoParams): TransactResult;
class TxnCache { constructor(capacity = 1000); get(id); set(id, result) }
staleConflicts(history: History, baseRevision: number, keys: string[]): StaleWrite | null;   // conflicts.ts
```

- Static validation (`validateOpsStatic`), before any transaction; failures throw `ProtocolFailure("bad_request", …)`: a binding (`as`, values of `owned`) is introduced at most once; every `$name` use comes after its introduction (op order); `owned` keys are plain ids; `base_revision` is an integer between 0 and the current revision; `actor` is present only when `ctx.kind` is not `agent`, and is `{type:"character", id}` naming an existing object whose `is_character` is true; `label` ≤ 200 characters.
- Idempotency: with `txn_id`, a cached result for that id is returned unchanged without executing; `TxnCache` keeps the last 1,000 results (insertion order, oldest evicted), committed and rejected alike.
- Execution: one `transactWithDice(table, actor, {kind: "edit", label}, ctx.dice, fn)` (vtt-75c.15), actor = `params.actor ?? ctx.actor`. Inside `fn` ops run in order. Bindings: `as` on `create_object` binds the created id, `as` on `spawn` the root copy, `owned` maps template-subtree ids to their copies (from spawn's returned copy map). `$name` in id positions and refs inside values (deep: lists, viewers entries) are replaced by the bound id, and replaced values are re-checked with `isValue`. Mapping: `set_value` → `writeValue`; `set_formula` → `setFormula`; `clear_override` → `clearOverride`; `delete_cell` → `deleteCell`; `rename_cell` → `renameCell`; `set_cell_visibility` → `setCellVisibility`; `set_tag` → `setTag`; `set_shape` → `setShape`; `set_template_flag` → `setTemplateFlag`; `set_character_flag` → `setCharacterFlag`; `reorder` → `reorder`; `add_board` → `addBoard`; `rename_board` → `renameBoard` (vtt-75c.14); `set_actions` → `setActions`; `remove_board` → `removeBoard` (vtt-75c.18); `create_object` → `createObject(tx, init, to, id?)`; `spawn` → `spawn(tx, template, to, cells)`; `move` → `move`; `remove` → `remove` (vtt-75c.6). A `Rejected` thrown by op i is re-thrown annotated with `op_index: i` (0-based). Default label when none is given: the single op's type and target (`"set_value goblin1.hp"`), else `"<n> edits"`.
- Stale writes (PROTOCOL.md §6), checked inside `fn` after the last op and before returning, so a refusal aborts with nothing applied and no randomness consumed: if `base_revision` < current revision, K = union of `touchedKeys` over `tx.effects()`; the conflicting groups are the retained groups with `revision > base_revision` (undo groups included) whose touched keys intersect K (`obj:<id>` intersects every key on that object). If `base_revision` is lower than the `base_revision` of the oldest retained group, the check is impossible: `truncated: true`, refused. Any conflict throws `StaleWriteError`, caught after the abort and returned as `{status:"rejected", rejection: {type:"stale_write", base_revision, revision, truncated, conflicts: [{index, revision, actor, label, keys}]}}`, `keys` being each group's intersecting keys.
- Undo: `target.type: "mine"` becomes `{type:"actor", actor: ctx.actor}`; other targets pass through to vtt-75c.8's `undo(store, actor, selector)`. With `expect_index`, `findUndoTarget` runs first and a different target (or none) is refused `{type:"undo_target_changed", expected, actual}`. Undo takes no `base_revision` and is not stale-checked.
- Result: committed → `revision`, group `index`, `created` (one entry per `create_object`), `copies` (one per `spawn`), `bindings`. Rejected → the `Rejection` or protocol rejection, with `op_index` when an op refused. Any other error propagates unchanged (the router reports it as `internal`).

Done when: tests on a `Table` built in the test show: each of the 19 op kinds commits and has the M2 effect (one test per op, checking stored state); a batch `create_object fb_aldric` (as `$card`), `create_object` zone into `$card`'s contents (as `$zone`), `set_value fb_aldric.zone {type:"ref", object:"$zone"}` commits as one group and the stored ref is the real id; `spawn` with `owned` returns bindings for the root and the owned copies; a use before introduction, a duplicate binding and `base_revision` above current are `bad_request` with no group; a protected write in the second of three ops is rejected with `op_index: 1` and nothing applied; GM writes `goblin1.hp` taking revision 5 to 6, then an agent transact with `base_revision: 5` writing `goblin1.hp` is `stale_write` naming that group and key `cell:goblin1/hp`, while one writing `goblin1.ac` commits; a stale `move` into a container conflicts with an intervening reorder of that container; a stale write to an object removed since conflicts through `obj:`; `base_revision` older than the oldest retained group after `compactLog` is refused with `truncated: true`; a refused stale write consumes no dice (a `ScriptedDiceSource` keeps its entry); the same `txn_id` twice returns the identical result and appends one group; the cache evicts the oldest entry after 1,000; `undo {type:"mine"}` by the agent skips a later GM group; an `expect_index` mismatch is `undo_target_changed`; an agent context passing `actor` is `bad_request`; a UI context acting as Aldric records actor `{type:"character", id:"aldric"}`; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: transport and message parsing (vtt-5su.10); views and events (vtt-5su.6, vtt-5su.9); `invoke` and roll steps (M5); `beside`/`table` destinations (M5).

Depends on: vtt-5su.3, vtt-75c.18, vtt-75c.6, vtt-75c.8, vtt-75c.12, vtt-75c.15.

title: Authority: table host (open, lock, autosave, save)
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 Persistence (autosave cadence, atomic saves with two failure stages, hand edits), §8.4 steps 1, 6, 15; docs/PROTOCOL.md §2 (new table, lock file) as written by vtt-5su.2.

Exclusive files: `packages/authority/src/host/table-host.ts`, `lock.ts`, `new-table.ts`, tests `test/host/*.test.ts`; sorted lines `export * from "./host/lock"`, `"./host/new-table"`, `"./host/table-host"` in `packages/authority/src/index.ts`.

- `TableHost.open(path, {createIfMissing = false, dice?: DiceSource, autosave = {debounceMs: 2000, maxDelayMs: 10000} | false, clock?, fs?}): Promise<TableHost>`: acquires the lock, then `loadTable(path)` (vtt-75c.17) or, when the file is missing and `createIfMissing`, `newTableSnapshot()` (one board `gm_board` named "GM", no objects, revision 0, empty log) followed by an immediate save; missing without `createIfMissing` is an error naming the path. Exposes `table` (vtt-75c.12 `Table.fromStore`), `dice` (default vtt-75c.15 `RandomDiceSource` seeded from `crypto.getRandomValues`), `path`, `warnings: string[]` (missing assets, `editedExternally`), `revision`, `lastSavedRevision`.
- `TableHost.inMemory(store, {dice?}): TableHost`: no file, no lock, no autosave; `save()` returns `{status: "failed", message: "no file"}`.
- Lock (`lock.ts`, `FileLock`): `<path>.lock` created with flag `wx`, content `{pid, started_at}`. An existing lock whose pid is alive (`process.kill(pid, 0)` succeeds) → `TableLockedError`; a dead pid → replaced, with a warning. Released on `close()`.
- Autosave: after each commit (via the store's public `onCommit`), schedule a save `debounceMs` after the latest commit, but no later than `maxDelayMs` after the first unsaved commit. `save()` saves now and cancels the schedule. Saves run through `saveTable`; the result maps to `saved` (ok), `saved_not_durable` (stage `after_replace`), `failed` (stage `before_replace`; the next scheduled save retries, and a failed save keeps the revision unsaved), and is emitted to `onSave(listener)` as `{status, revision, message?}`. A revision already saved is not saved again. No automatic compaction.
- `close()`: cancels timers, saves if `revision !== lastSavedRevision`, releases the lock; idempotent.

Done when: tests with fake timers and a temp directory show: opening a missing path with `createIfMissing` writes a loadable file with the GM board; without it, an error naming the path; a second `open` on the same path while the first holds the lock throws `TableLockedError`; a stale lock (pid of an exited child process) is taken over with a warning; three commits 500 ms apart produce one save 2 s after the last; commits every second produce a save at 10 s; `save()` saves immediately and cancels the pending one; a fault-injected `before_replace` failure emits `failed` and the next scheduled save succeeds; an `after_replace` failure emits `saved_not_durable`; `close()` saves unsaved work and releases the lock, and reopening shows the same snapshot and log (indices, barrier); a hand-edited file opens with an `editedExternally` warning; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: the server (vtt-5su.10); compaction policy (Polish); stocking the GM binder with example templates (M5); asset import (M4); in-memory checkpoints (Polish).

Depends on: vtt-5su.2, vtt-75c.12, vtt-75c.15, vtt-75c.17.

title: Protocol: wire schemas and types (@vtt/protocol)
Docs: protocol, MCP and authority-process decisions
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.4, §5.2, §7, §10; FORMULAS.md §7; new docs/PROTOCOL.md; CLAUDE.md package list. Planning bead vtt-5su.1 (plan accepted with the orchestrator's amendments).

Docs only; the only M3 bead that edits docs. Writes down the decisions below so every later M3 bead cites a doc section. One decision-log row in DESIGN §10 per numbered decision (D1–D31), dated the commit day. Wire field names and the method and op tables are copied exactly from vtt-5su.3's description.

Decisions to record:

- D1 Process model: one authority process per table (`vtt-serve <file>`) owns the file and the M2 `Table` and serves the protocol over a WebSocket. The MCP server is a separate stdio process (`vtt-mcp`) launched by the agent host; it attaches to the running authority as a protocol client with an `agent` actor. The authority package ships the MCP server (DESIGN §7's "hosts the MCP server" becomes "ships").
- D2 Package: new `@vtt/protocol` (wire schemas, `ProtocolClient`, `ViewMirror`), browser-safe, depends only on `@vtt/schema` and zod; used by authority, MCP server and M4's UI.
- D3 Transport: JSON text frames on one WebSocket at `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/ws`; envelope tagged by `type` (`hello`, `welcome`, `request`, `response`, `event`, `goodbye`); client-chosen string request ids echoed in responses; exact-match `protocol: 1` in `hello`. The wire format lives in docs/PROTOCOL.md.
- D4 Auth: bind 127.0.0.1 only; a random 256-bit token per server start, required in `hello`; WebSocket upgrades with an `Origin` other than the server's own origin or an `--allow-origin` entry are refused with 403. Every authenticated connection has GM authority; `viewer` is a view-as selector, not a security boundary, in v1.
- D5 Discovery: `vtt-serve` writes `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/vtt/session.json` (`{url, token, pid, table}`, mode 0600); `vtt-mcp` uses `--url/--token`, else `VTT_URL`/`VTT_TOKEN`, else that file; the last started authority wins.
- D6 Commands: one write command `transact` carrying a list of ops (19 kinds, one per M2 primitive including `set_actions` and `remove_board`) applied in one transaction = one group = one undo unit, with batch-local `$name` bindings (from `as` and `owned`) usable in op id positions and in ref values; plus `undo`, `save`, `invoke`.
- D7 Stale writes: every `transact` carries `base_revision`; it is refused `stale_write` iff a group committed after `base_revision` (undo groups included) shares a touched key (the undo-conflict keys of DESIGN §7) with the transaction's own effects, or `base_revision` predates the retained history (`truncated`). Disjoint writes commit; nothing is rebased or re-evaluated. Undo is not stale-checked and may pin its target with `expect_index` (`undo_target_changed`). This replaces "the policy for stale writes belongs to M3's protocol" in §7.
- D8 Retries: optional `txn_id`; the authority remembers the last 1,000 results in memory and returns the stored result for a repeat.
- D9 Actors: `client.kind: "agent"` → `{type:"agent", name}`; `ui` and `test` → `gm`; non-agent connections may pass `actor: {type:"character", id}` per `transact` (the GM driving a character); agents cannot.
- D10 Subscriptions: per connection, each with a scope (`board` incl. contents recursively, `objects` with optional subtree, `all`, `log`) and a viewer; `subscribe` returns full views; afterwards one `commit` event per commit per connection with the group header and, per subscription, upserted whole object views, removed ids, cover changes and (log scope) group views. After each commit the authority pulls exactly the dirty cells inside some subscription's scope and sends changed views; other dirty cells stay dirty (FORMULAS §7 gains this sentence).
- D11 Cell views: GM views carry value, kind, formula source, override flag, per-cell visibility entry and full actions; character views carry value, kind, override flag and action names only, never formula source. Every readable structural cell (with defaults) is part of a view's `cells`.
- D12 Redaction: in character views a ref (top level, in lists, in viewers values) to an object the viewer cannot see is the wire-only value `{type:"redacted"}` in place, so contents keep their count; an error whose origin the viewer cannot see keeps only its code.
- D13 Face-down exemptions are vtt-75c.10's `FACE_DOWN_EXEMPT` (no row here; DESIGN §4.4 already says so). Reference it in PROTOCOL.md §7 only.
- D14 Covers: character views carry, per board in scope, a `Cover` (region: position, rotation, shape; or `whole_board` for an undetermined zone) for each opaque zone the viewer cannot see, keyed so the zone id is not revealed; the zone and covered objects are absent.
- D15 Log filtering for characters is by current visibility: names and effects limited to what the viewer can see now, effects on removed objects dropped, groups with nothing left omitted, header kept.
- D16 Explain: `explain_cell` returns content (source, override, whether it parses), the recorded dependency tree to depth ≤ 4 and ≤ 200 nodes with values (for characters: hidden cells named without value, invisible objects as `object: null`), the error-origin chain and the last writing group; `explain_group` returns effects plus the origin action's current definition; `explain_action` returns the `when` source, value and enabled state, and step text.
- D17 MCP tools: `table_info`, `list_objects`, `get_objects`, `evaluate`, `zones`, `at_position`, `changes_since`, `log`, `explain_cell`, `explain_group`, `explain_action`, `transact`, `undo`, `save`, `subscribe`, `poll_changes`, `unsubscribe`; input schemas generated from the protocol schemas; rejected writes return `isError: true`; resources `vtt://docs/formulas`, `vtt://docs/design`, `vtt://docs/protocol`, `vtt://schema/ops`.
- D18 MCP subscribe: a change buffer per subscription in the MCP process, drained by `poll_changes` (long poll ≤ 30 s), plus `notifications/resources/updated` on `vtt://subscriptions/<id>`; cap 1,000 commits, then `overflowed`.
- D19 `invoke` is part of protocol v1 and answered `unsupported` until M5; M5 adds its MCP tool together with the UI's buttons.
- D20 Actions are defined by the `setActions` primitive (vtt-75c.18; its own rows) — referenced, no row here.
- D21 Limits: `max_message_bytes` 1 MiB, `max_ops` 1,000, `max_page` 200, `max_ids` 200, `max_subscriptions` 16, `max_explain_depth` 4, `max_explain_nodes` 200, `max_source_length` 10,000, `max_groups` 500, `max_requests_per_second` 200 (`busy`), `max_buffered_bytes` 8 MiB (slow consumer closed 4429). Formula cost stays under the engine budget.
- D22 Ordering: the authority handles messages one at a time in arrival order; commits are totally ordered by revision; every connection receives every commit event in revision order; the committer receives the commit event before its response.
- D23 Reconnection: no server-side resumption; the client re-sends `hello`, resubscribes and replaces its mirrors with full views (`resync`); pending requests fail `disconnected`; ping every 15 s, two missed pongs terminate.
- D24 Autosave: 2 s after the last commit, at most 10 s after the first unsaved commit, on `save`, and on shutdown; failures retry at the next schedule and are broadcast; no automatic compaction in v1 (DESIGN §7 "autosave cadence is M3's" is replaced by this).
- D25 New table and files: a missing file is created with one board `gm_board` named "GM" and no objects; default port 4747; lock file `<file>.lock`.
- D26 Step 5 acceptance writes the hatch as an ordinary cell `pattern: "hatch"` (M4 decides appearance cells) and authors the Fireball card from scratch.
- D27 Runtime dependencies: `ws` 8.22.0 (+ `@types/ws` 8.18.2), `@modelcontextprotocol/server` 2.3.1 (+ `@modelcontextprotocol/client` 2.3.1 for tests), `tsx` 4.23.15 to run the binaries, `zod` 4.6.7. Add a CLAUDE.md line: new runtime dependencies are pinned exactly and recorded in the decision log.
- D28 `evaluate` (ad hoc formulas) is GM-only.
- D29 `at_position`: objects directly on the board whose evaluated footprint contains the point (boundary inclusive; shapeless: anchor within epsilon), zones listed separately, both ascending `z` then id; contained objects excluded.
- D30 A GM-only `document` method returns the canonical snapshot and retained log; no MCP tool.
- D31 Board removal is `removeBoard` (vtt-75c.18) — referenced, no row here.

Doc edits:

- docs/PROTOCOL.md (new): §1 transport, framing, envelope, close codes (D3); §2 hello, auth, origin, discovery, new table (D4, D5, D25); §3 actors (D9); §4 methods with params and results field by field; §5 ops, their M2 primitives, bindings (D6); §6 revisions, stale writes, retries (D7, D8); §7 views, redaction, covers, face-down exemptions, log filtering (D11–D15); §8 subscriptions, commit events, ordering, reconnection (D10, D22, D23); §9 explain, evaluate, at_position, document (D16, D28–D30); §10 errors and limits (D21); §11 MCP tools, resources, change polling (D17–D19); §12 additive-extension rule (M5 adds `invoke` behaviour and face fields additively).
- DESIGN.md §5.2: D1, the tool groups, D7, D21 and the view-as note of D4.
- DESIGN.md §7: Platform paragraph (D1, D2); Revisions (D7); Persistence (D24, D25); a short **Protocol** paragraph pointing to PROTOCOL.md.
- DESIGN.md §4.4: D12, D14, D15, D16 (filtering of query results, explain and the log).
- FORMULAS.md §7 Propagation: "After each commit the authority recomputes the dirty cells that some subscription's view includes and sends those whose view changed; other dirty cells stay dirty until read."
- CLAUDE.md: `protocol` in the package list (D2); the dependency line (D27).

Done when: every edit above is present; DESIGN §10 has one row per decision D1–D31 except D13, D20 and D31; PROTOCOL.md's method table (17 methods) and op table (19 ops) match vtt-5su.3's description; no code changes; `pnpm format:check` and `pnpm lint` exit 0.

Out of scope: any code; the M2 docs; vtt-75c.18's two rows; face layouts and action syntax (M5); asset naming and appearance cells (M4).

Depends on: none.

title: Authority: setActions and removeBoard primitives
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §5.2 ("define … actions"), §4.3 (boards), §4.5, §7 (operation records, undo conflict keys, identity); FORMULAS.md §8 (an action has a name, an optional precondition, and a list of steps); DESIGN.md §4.1 Identity (board ids are reserved for the document's lifetime).

Two edit primitives M2 lacks, needed by the M3 protocol (vtt-5su) and the M4/M5 UI. Additive changes to M2 files after their owning beads merge: `packages/schema/src/ops.ts` (vtt-75c.4), `packages/authority/src/store/effects.ts` and `summary.ts` (vtt-75c.5), `store/edits.ts` (vtt-75c.14). Tests in `test/store/actions-boards.test.ts`; the vtt-75c.5 effect round-trip test gains an `actions` example.

- Schema: the `field` effect's `field` union gains `"actions"`, with `before`/`after` of type `ActionDef[]`.
- effects.ts: `applyEffect`, `historicalInverse`/`applyHistoricalInverse` and `invertForUndo` handle `field: "actions"` (exact reversal); `touchedKeys` returns `actions:<obj>` (intersected by `obj:<id>` like every key on that object); `changedCells` returns nothing (actions are not readable cells).
- summary.ts: `ChangeSummary.actionsChanged: ObjectId[]`, deduplicated, filled by `SummaryBuilder` from `field: "actions"` effects.
- `setActions(tx, obj, actions: ActionDef[])` in edits.ts: replaces the object's whole action list with one field effect. Refused as `invalid` (vtt-75c.4 `Rejection`) when the object does not exist, an action name is empty or longer than 100 characters, two actions share a name (exact comparison), or `steps` is not an array of strings. `when` and step text are stored verbatim and not parsed (M5 owns step syntax). Spawn already copies actions (vtt-75c.6); no change there.
- `removeBoard(tx, id)` in edits.ts: refused as `invalid` when the board does not exist or any object is directly on it; otherwise records a `board` effect with `after: null` and a `retire` of the board id. title: Authority: atomic save/load I/O and epic acceptance
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 Persistence ("Saves are atomic"; assets beside the file), §8.4 steps 6 and 15, with the save-failure and asset rules written by vtt-75c.2; the epic M2 done-when ("a document round-trips through the file format and undo of an op group is refused correctly after a conflicting op").

Filesystem I/O on top of vtt-75c.11's pure serialization, plus the epic acceptance test. Exclusive files: packages/authority/src/persist/io.ts (one added export line in src/persist/index.ts), test/epic-m2.test.ts, test/persist/io.test.ts.

- `saveTable(path, store, assets, fs = nodeFs)`: `serializeTable`, then writes `<path>.tmp-<pid>-<random>` in the same directory, fsyncs it, renames over `path`, then fsyncs the directory (ignoring `EISDIR`/`EPERM` on platforms that refuse directory fsync). Two failure stages: a failure before the rename (write, file fsync, rename) removes the temp file, leaves the original byte-identical, and returns `{ok: false, stage: "before_replace", error}`; a failure of the directory fsync after the rename leaves the new file in place and intact and returns `{ok: false, stage: "after_replace", error}` ("saved, durability not confirmed"). Success returns `{ok: true}`. `fs` is injectable for fault tests.
- `loadTable(path, fs = nodeFs)`: reads the file and calls `parseTable`; then checks each asset path, resolved against the file's directory, for existence through `fs`; missing assets are warnings in the result, not errors.

test/epic-m2.test.ts: build a document with a board, a goblin and a spawned card holding a zone; apply a set, an override, a move, a spawn, a remove and an undo; save to a temp directory; load; `toSnapshot()` and the log (indices, `first_index`, barrier) deep-equal the originals; then on the loaded store the GM writes a cell, the agent writes the same cell, and `undo({type:"actor", actor: gm})` is refused with `undo_conflict`, while `undo({type:"latest"})` succeeds.

title: Authority: document store, transactions, replay
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 (document plus ordered op stream, transactions, commit point, internal synchronization before notifications, error handling, change summary, replay and rewind), as written by vtt-75c.2; FORMULAS.md §8.1 (atomicity); FIXTURES.md §8 (one group per committed step).

The transactional store over vtt-75c.5's `DocState`, effects, summary and `History`. Exclusive files in packages/authority/src/store/: document-store.ts, transaction.ts, replay.ts, compare.ts (export lines added to src/store/index.ts without reordering others).

- document-store.ts: `DocumentStore.fromSnapshot(snapshot, history?)` (validated with `validateSnapshot`), `toSnapshot()` (deep copy, canonical order: objects by id, cells and `cell_visibility` by name), the `DocState` read API, `revision`, `history`.
- transaction.ts: `store.begin(actor, {kind, label, origin?, undoes?})` returns a `Transaction`; one transaction at a time (`begin` while one is open throws). `tx.record(effect)` applies the effect to a working copy and appends it; `tx.doc` is the working copy's read API; `tx.changes()` is the live `ChangeSummary` so far. `commit()`: validates the working document with `validateSnapshot` (failure → `Rejected({type:"invalid"})`, nothing published); captures `names` (working-copy names for touched objects; for removed objects, the name just before removal); builds the `OpGroup` (`base_revision`, `revision = base_revision + 1`, `undoes`); then the commit point: the new document and the appended group are published atomically. Immediately after the commit point, internal synchronization hooks (`store.onCommitInternal(fn)`, run in registration order; used by the engine adapter and the index) run, then public `store.onCommit` listeners. Both receive the payload `{group, summary: ChangeSummary, before: DocState (read-only view of the pre-commit document)}`. An error thrown by a public listener is collected and reported (`commit()` returns `{group, summary, listenerErrors}`) and never undoes or aborts the commit; an error in an internal hook is a bug and propagates after the commit is published. `abort()` discards everything. A refusing primitive throws `Rejected` (carries a `Rejection`).
- `store.transact(actor, meta, fn)`: runs `fn(tx)`; a `Rejected` thrown before the commit point aborts and returns `{ok: false, rejection}`; any other error thrown before the commit point aborts and is rethrown unchanged (scenario errors stay scenario errors); success returns `{ok: true, group, summary, listenerErrors}`. An `onAbort` hook lets callers (the dice wrapper in vtt-75c.15) reset state on either pre-commit failure. A committed group with no effects is still a group.
- replay.ts: `replay(base, groups)`: applies each group's effects in order and sets `revision` to each group's `revision` (also for no-effect groups); requires `base.revision === groups[0].base_revision`. `rewind(head, groups)`: applies `applyHistoricalInverse` of each effect, groups and effects in reverse order, setting `revision` to each group's `base_revision`. Neither touches dice or evaluation.
- compare.ts: `storedStateEqual(a, b, {ignoreRevision = true, ignoreIdentity = false})` and `diffStoredState` (for messages): compare canonical snapshots, excluding `revision` by default and, with `ignoreIdentity`, `next_seq` and `retired_ids`. Shared by vtt-75c.8, vtt-75c.11 and the runner's `replay` expectation (vtt-75c.13).

Done when: tests (test/store/document-store.test.ts, transaction.test.ts, replay.test.ts, compare.test.ts) show: `fromSnapshot`/`toSnapshot` round-trip; `begin` while a transaction is open throws; a transaction whose working document fails validation on commit leaves no trace (document, history, revision); one committed transaction appends exactly one group with the next absolute index and increments `revision` by one; group `names` hold the name at commit time even after a later rename, and a removed object's name; the commit payload's summary matches the effects (spawn, same-value write, move with derived keys, remove) and `before` shows the pre-commit state; internal hooks run before public listeners, including a public listener registered before the internal hook was added; a throwing public listener does not abort the commit and is reported in `listenerErrors`; `transact` returns a rejection for `Rejected`, rethrows a `ScenarioError`-like custom error unchanged after aborting, and calls `onAbort` in both cases but not after a commit whose listener throws; `replay` from a base snapshot at revision 7 through groups including a no-effect group reproduces the head including `revision`, and `rewind` reproduces the base including `revision`, `next_seq` and `retired_ids`; `storedStateEqual` ignores `revision` by default and identity only when asked; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-75c.2); effects, summary, history (vtt-75c.5); edit and structural primitives (vtt-75c.14, vtt-75c.6); undo selection (vtt-75c.8); persistence (vtt-75c.11, vtt-75c.17); formula evaluation (vtt-75c.12).

Depends on: vtt-75c.5.


Note from vtt-75c.5 as merged: `historicalInverse(effect, stateBefore)` takes the state before the effect (the inverse of a board removal records the board's index), so inverses cannot be derived while rewinding backward from a later state. The store computes each group's historical inverses while applying or replaying forward and keeps them in memory (never persisted), or rewinds by replaying from a snapshot. `History` returns deep-frozen records (`FrozenGroup`, `DeepReadonly<TableLog>`); copy before mutating.

title: Formula: engine integration (budget, spatial callbacks, ad hoc evaluation, exception recovery)
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §7 (query dependencies, budget, host-independence), §6 (spatial functions in the engine), §8.1 (`when` as an ordinary formula), §2.3 (#LIMIT), as written by vtt-o9i.12; DESIGN.md §7 (budgets, responsiveness).

Complete the engine on top of vtt-o9i.9's core. Exclusive files: packages/formula/src/engine/env.ts (the recording `EvalEnv`'s query methods), budget.ts, adhoc.ts (export lines added to src/index.ts without reordering). Tests test/engine-integration-*.test.ts with `MemoryHost` (vtt-o9i.15) and the queries of vtt-o9i.8.

- Query methods. The engine's `EvalEnv` implements `objectsOnBoard(board, near)` by calling `host.objectsOnBoard(board, near)` (the host never evaluates; the candidate set is defined over literal geometry) and records an `{index}` dependency; `allObjects` and `objectsNamed` likewise record `{index}`. Geometry of candidates is read by the evaluator through the ordinary recording `read`, so formula positions are cell dependencies and can close a cycle (vtt-o9i.9's cycle rules apply).
- Budget. Each formula evaluation (final attempt) may spend `options.budget` (default 20,000): each cell read, each existence check, each candidate tested by a spatial query, and each id returned by `allObjects`/`objectsNamed` costs 1; reading an already computed dependency costs 1 regardless of its own cost. Because the candidate set is host-independent, the charge is the same on every host. Exceeding the budget gives #LIMIT (origin itself); dependents see the propagated error. Results never depend on cache state or read order.
- Ad hoc. `engine.evaluate(source, {thisId})` parses and evaluates with the same recording env (reads use and populate the memo) but keeps no dependency entry for itself; it is how `when` guards and show-when are evaluated.
- Host exceptions propagate out of `value`/`evaluate`; the engine first resets every in-progress cell (and the work stack) to dirty, so the engine stays usable.

Done when: tests show: a zone's `contents(this)` cell recomputes after `MemoryHost.move` brings an object it never returned into the zone, and after `createObject` places one inside; `obj("Goblin")` changes after a `set` of the goblin's `name`; a cycle through a spatial query (a token whose formula `position` depends on the `contents(...)` of a zone it is a candidate of) is #CYCLE and recovers after `replaceContent`; `objects(…)` over 30 objects with `budget: 50` is #LIMIT while a sibling cell is fine; budget-limited results are identical cold, warm and in reversed read order; host equivalence: with a deliberately small budget, the same formulas give identical results and identical #LIMIT outcomes on `MemoryHost` (brute force) and on a test-only grid-indexed host computing the same literal-geometry candidate set, including objects with formula positions, a candidate whose position formula is an error, and a cycle through geometry; `engine.evaluate("hit and dmg = empty", {thisId})` for the attack card's guards; a host that throws mid-evaluation leaves the engine usable and the next read correct; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-o9i.12); the core resolution, memo, graph and cycles (vtt-o9i.9); query semantics (vtt-o9i.8); finer index keys (Polish); action reads (vtt-75c.15).

description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §3.1 (structural defaults, landing rule, literal-only `name` and `tag`), §6 (the literal-geometry candidate set), as written by vtt-o9i.12 and vtt-75c.2; docs/FIXTURES.md §3 (setup), §6 (`move` destinations).

`MemoryHost`: the mutable test document every engine, runner and acceptance test in M1 uses. Exclusive file: packages/formula/test/support/memory-host.ts. It implements vtt-o9i.3's `EvalHost`.

- `MemoryHost.fromSetup(setup)`: cells from `cells` (literals as-is, `{type:"formula"}` as formula content); structural cells derived as FIXTURES §3 says (`id`, `tag`, `contents`, derived `container`, `board` and `position` from `placement`, `shape` as a ShapeValue, `is_zone`), every other §3.1 cell defaulted per vtt-o9i.3's table; a formula in `name` or `tag` is a setup error (thrown); ids in `setup.characters` get `is_character`. Boards `exists()` and have no cells.
- `objectsOnBoard(board, near)`: the candidate set by brute force over literal geometry, exactly as vtt-o9i.3's contract defines it: objects directly on the board whose literal `indexBounds` (vtt-75c.7) intersect `near` (`boundsIntersect`), plus every object on the board with a formula-valued `position`, `rotation`, `z` or `shape` (no override). Never evaluates formulas. Also exported as `literalCandidates(host, board, near)`, the reference other hosts are tested against.
- Test-only mutators, each returning the `Change[]` to feed `engine.invalidate`, covering every cell whose content changed, including derived `container` and both containers' `contents`:
  - `set(id, cell, value)` (creates an absent cell); `override(id, cell, value)`; `clearOverride(id, cell)`; `replaceContent(id, cell, content)` (literal or formula; drops any override; a formula on `name` or `tag` throws).
  - `move(id, dest)`, `dest` a FIXTURES §6 board destination `{board, position}` or container destination `{container, index}`, with the landing rules of FORMULAS §3.1: leaves its old container's `contents` or board; container destination inserts at `index` (default append) and deletes `position`, `rotation`, `z`; board destination sets `board`, empties `container`, writes `position` as a literal (as an override if it holds a formula), sets `z` to 1 + the maximum literal `z` of the other objects on that board (absent or empty as 0) unless `z` holds a formula, keeps `rotation` on board-to-board moves; `owner` never changes.

  - `deleteObject(id)`: recursive over `contents`; returns `object_deleted` for every removed object plus the surviving parent's `contents` change.
  - `isOverridden(id, cell)`.

title: Authority: action context and dice sources
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §8.1 ("Reads inside an action"), §2.2 and §8.3 (`roll`, `shuffle` as the only randomness), as written by vtt-75c.2; FIXTURES.md §5 (the dice script: order, normalized `expr` match, permutation, atomicity, exhaustion and leftover as scenario errors).

Exclusive files: packages/authority/src/engine/action-context.ts, dice.ts (export lines added to src/engine/index.ts without reordering others).

action-context.ts, `ActionContext(table, tx)` for M5: implements vtt-o9i.3's `EvalEnv` over a committed `Table` and an open transaction (vtt-75c.16), using the transaction's live change summary `tx.changes()` and working copy `tx.doc`. Reads, in this order:

1. Transaction-local existence: an object removed earlier in `tx` does not exist (`exists` false; any read of it is #REF, even if it was written before its removal); an object that neither exists at the start of the action nor was created in `tx` does not exist.
2. An object created in `tx` (spawned or created): its cells read from the working copy: a literal reads as the literal; a cell with an override reads as the override (copied overrides included); structural cells read from the working copy with structural defaults; a formula cell without override reads `empty` (formulas are not evaluated before commit).
3. An existing object: a cell whose stored state was changed in `tx` (as listed in `tx.changes()`: written cells, including same-value writes, and move-derived cells) reads from the working copy: a literal or override as written; structural and move-derived cells (`board`, `position`, `rotation`, `z`, `container`, `contents`, `tag`, `shape`) as they now stand; a cell whose content was replaced by a formula in `tx` reads `empty`.
4. Any other cell reads as of the start of the action: `table.value` (still the pre-action value, because recompute runs only after commit).

Query and existence methods complete the `EvalEnv` contract against the working copy: `exists` by rule 1 (created and removed objects from `tx.changes()`); `objectsNamed` and `allObjects` over working-copy objects (literal names); `objectsOnBoard(board, near)` returns the literal-geometry candidate set (FORMULAS §6) computed by brute force over the working copy's literal geometry, never evaluating formulas (an index reflects only committed state); candidate geometry is then read by the evaluator through this context's reads, so the candidate set and budget equal what any host would give for that state.

dice.ts: `DiceSource { roll(dice): RollValue; permutation(n): number[]; mark(): number; reset(mark): void }`.
- `RandomDiceSource(seed)`: a seedable PRNG implemented in this file (a small, documented generator such as sfc32 or xoshiro128**) whose whole state is copyable; `mark()` returns a copy of the state and `reset(mark)` restores it, so after a reset the source behaves exactly as if the aborted draws never happened, whatever ranges are requested next. Range mapping is unbiased (rejection sampling). Rolling uses vtt-o9i.13's `rollDice` through a `RandomSource` adapter; permutations use Fisher–Yates on the same generator.
- `ScriptedDiceSource(entries)`: hands out FIXTURES §5 entries in order, throwing `ScenarioError` on exhaustion, kind mismatch, or an `expr` not equal to the requested dice by vtt-o9i.5's `diceEquals`; `mark`/`reset` move its position; `remaining()`.
- `rollInto(tx, source, obj, cell, dice)` = `source.roll` then vtt-75c.14's `rollWrite(tx, …)`; `shuffleWith(tx, source, container)` = `source.permutation(len)` then `reorder(tx, …)`.
- `transactWithDice(table, actor, meta, source, fn)` (exported from this file, so table.ts is not edited): marks the source, then runs `store.transact` with an `onAbort` that resets it. A `Rejected` before the commit point returns the rejection; any other error before the commit point (including `ScenarioError` from a scripted source) aborts, resets the source, and propagates unchanged; after the commit point the source is never reset, even if a public listener throws. So a refused or aborted transaction consumes no randomness and no script entries.

Done when: tests show: `ActionContext` reads written values; start-of-action values for unwritten formula cells even after a write to their input; `empty` for a formula cell on an object spawned in the same transaction; a copied literal and a copied override on a spawned object read as copied; after a move in `tx`, the moved object's `position`, `board`, `container` and both containers' `contents` read as moved; write → remove → read of the same object gives #REF; `exists` of a removed and of a created object; `objectsOnBoard` includes a spawned object and excludes a removed one; the scripted source matches `1d8+3` against a request equal by normalization, throws on mismatch and exhaustion, and is reset after an aborted transaction; `RandomDiceSource`: an aborted transaction containing a `1d20` roll and a shuffle of 5, followed by a `3d6` roll, a `1d100` roll and a shuffle of 3, yields exactly the same results as a control run that performs only the latter three; a refused transaction behaves the same; a `ScenarioError` thrown inside `transactWithDice` propagates unchanged and the scripted source is reset; a committed transaction whose public listener throws keeps its consumed entries; seeded runs are deterministic; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-75c.2); the action runner (`when`, steps, `each`, step errors: M5); the host adapter and recompute (vtt-75c.12); cryptographic randomness.

title: Authority: cell, field, reorder and board edit primitives
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.1 (cells), §4.2 (literals, formulas, overrides), §4.4 (per-cell visibility metadata); FORMULAS.md §3.1 (protected cells; literal-only `name` and `tag`; edit-only `shape`), §8.2 ("Writing to a cell that holds a formula creates an override… Writing to a protected cell is an error"), as written by vtt-75c.2 and vtt-o9i.12; FIXTURES.md §6 (`set`, `override`, `clear_override` meanings).

The edit primitives over vtt-75c.16's transactions. Each primitive is a function taking the open `Transaction` as its first argument and recording effects through `tx.record`, so no bead edits transaction.ts after vtt-75c.16. Exclusive files: packages/authority/src/store/edits.ts (re-exported through one added line in src/store/index.ts). Tests: test/store/edits.test.ts.

- `writeValue(tx, obj, cell, value)`: literal or absent cell becomes that literal; a formula cell gets `override = value`. Absent cells are created (FIXTURES §6 `set`).
- `setFormula(tx, obj, cell, source)`: replaces content with a formula, dropping any override.
- `clearOverride(tx, obj, cell)`: removes the override; `invalid` if none.
- `deleteCell(tx, obj, cell)`; `renameCell(tx, obj, from, to)`: refuses with `protected_cell` if `from` or `to` is any FORMULAS §3.1 structural name; refuses with `invalid` if `from` is absent or `to` exists; otherwise deletes and creates in one group (formulas naming the old name are not rewritten); per-cell visibility: any `cell_visibility` entry already recorded for the absent `to` is replaced by `from`'s entry, or removed if `from` has none, and `from`'s entry is removed.
- `setCellVisibility(tx, obj, cell, viewers | null)`: writes the per-object `cell_visibility` metadata (`cell_visibility` effect); valid for any cell name, including structural, field-backed, derived, and absent cells; `viewers` must be a non-empty literal viewers value (else `type_error`).
- `rollWrite(tx, obj, cell, roll)`: as `writeValue` with `cause: "roll"`.
- `setTag(tx, obj, tags)`, `setShape(tx, obj, shape | null)`, `setTemplateFlag(tx, obj, bool)`, `setCharacterFlag(tx, obj, bool)` (`field` effects).
- `reorder(tx, container, permutation)`: `new[i] = old[permutation[i]]` (FIXTURES §5); `invalid` unless a permutation of the length.
- `addBoard(tx, id, name?)`: `id` must satisfy `isValidId` and not be reserved (a live board, a live object, or retired; else `invalid`); records an `allocate` effect for the id (no `next_seq` change) and a `board` creation effect. `renameBoard(tx, id, name)` (`board` effect).

Protection and types: writing `id`, `board`, `is_zone`, `contents`, `container` through any cell primitive throws `protected_cell`; writing `shape` through `writeValue`, `setFormula` or `rollWrite` throws `protected_cell` (only `setShape` changes it); `template` and `name` accept literals only (`setFormula` on them is `type_error`); `tag` through `writeValue` must be a list of text and becomes a `setTag`, and `setFormula` on `tag` is `type_error`; `position` may be written only on a board object (else `protected_cell`); `opaque` only on zones; literal structural writes are type-checked against `STRUCTURAL_CELLS` (`type_error`). Deleting a structural cell is `protected_cell`.

Done when: tests show each primitive's effects and resulting state; `writeValue` on a formula cell creates an override and `clearOverride` restores formula tracking at the stored level; `clearOverride` without override is `invalid`; every protected write (including `writeValue` on `shape`) throws `protected_cell` and leaves the document and history unchanged; `setFormula` on `name`, `tag`, `template` is `type_error`; `setShape` changes the shape with a `field` effect; `setCellVisibility` on `contents` and on `tag` of an object with no such stored cells records a `cell_visibility` effect, and clearing it with `null` removes the entry; `renameCell` moves the visibility entry; `renameCell` to `container`, to `shape`, and from `name` are `protected_cell`; `renameCell` onto an existing cell is `invalid`; `renameCell` onto an absent cell that has its own `cell_visibility` entry replaces that entry with the source's (and removes it when the source has none); `addBoard` with an id used by a live object, by a live board, or retired is `invalid`, and a valid `addBoard` records `allocate` plus `board`; `reorder` with `[2,0,1]` on `[a,b,c]` gives `[c,a,b]`; a rename of `name` is captured in the next group's `names`; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.
