title: Formula: AST evaluation, scope, references, dispatch
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §2 (literals), §2.1 (`and`, `or`, `not` short-circuit), §2.2 (roll result fields), §2.3 (`iserror`, origin, arity, unknown names), §3 (bare names, `this`, `it`, dot-access, references), §5 (`if`), as written by vtt-o9i.12.

`evaluate(ast, scope, env): Result` over vtt-o9i.3's `EvalEnv`, using vtt-o9i.6's value semantics, plus the function-call machinery vtt-o9i.7 and vtt-o9i.8 plug into. Exclusive files: packages/formula/src/eval/scope.ts, evaluate.ts; src/functions/registry.ts, core.ts, library.ts and queries.ts (created as empty registrations, owned afterwards by vtt-o9i.7 and vtt-o9i.8), src/index.ts (add this bead's export lines and preserve the lines already added by the parser, dice, host-interface and value-semantics beads; never reorder or remove them). This bead also edits test/support/fake-env.ts once: `FakeEnv.read` passes each value through vtt-o9i.6's `validateRefs` with its own `exists`. Tests: test/eval-*.test.ts with `FakeEnv`.

- Literals. `Dice {raw}` → `parseDice`; error → #TYPE, else a dice value with normalized `expr`. `Viewer` → viewers `["all"]` / `["gm"]`. `Record` → #TYPE in a formula (records exist only as `spawn` arguments; M5 reads their fields from the AST). Lists evaluate items left to right and go through `collectList`.
- Operators dispatch to vtt-o9i.6's `binary`/`unary` (passing `chained`). A new error gets `origin = scope.cell` when the scope names a cell.
- `a and b`: evaluate `a`; error → it; falsy → `a`; else evaluate and return `b` unchanged. `a or b`: error → it; truthy → `a`; else `b`. `not x`: error → it; else boolean. `if(c, x, y)`: exactly 3 args; `c` error → it; evaluate only the chosen branch and return it unchanged (a roll stays a roll). None of these broadcast.
- `iserror(x)` (core.ts, flagged `acceptsErrors`): true iff `x` is an error.
- Names and scope. `scope = {thisId, it?, itBindsNames?, cell?}`. `this` → `ref(thisId)`. `it` outside where/sort/objects → #NAME. A bare name reads `env.read(thisId, name)`; inside a predicate (`itBindsNames`) bare names resolve only against the item's cells, and an item that is not a ref makes a bare name #TYPE; `it` works for any item. `read` returning `undefined` → #NAME.
- Dot-access. On a ref: deleted (`!env.exists`) → #REF; else the named cell, absent → #NAME. On `empty` → `empty`. On a roll result: `total`, `dice`, `dropped` (lists of numbers), `expr` (a dice value); any other name → #NAME. On a list: apply to each item and flatten one level. Anything else → #TYPE.
- Function calls. The registry is injectable: `createRegistry(defs)`; `coreRegistry()` holds only core.ts entries (`if`, `iserror`); the default registry used by the package is core plus whatever library.ts and queries.ts register; `evaluate(ast, scope, env, registry = defaultRegistry)`. `FunctionDef {name, minArgs, maxArgs, kind: "eager" | "lazy", broadcast: "none" | "scalar", acceptsErrors?, impl}`. Eager args are evaluated left to right, then error-checked, then `impl` runs; `broadcast: "scalar"` maps over list arguments (several must have equal length, else #TYPE). Lazy functions receive ASTs plus an evaluation callback (used by `if`, and by `where`/`sort`/`objects`). Arity mismatch → #TYPE; unknown function → #NAME. `Method` nodes dispatch to registry entries `where`/`sort`; an absent entry → #NAME.
- Recursion is over the AST only and is bounded by the parser's depth limit (256) from vtt-o9i.4; `evaluate` must not overflow the JS stack on any AST the parser accepts.

Done when: tests cover every bullet (and must remain valid after vtt-o9i.7 and vtt-o9i.8 register their functions), at least: `nickname or name` default; `if(bonus = empty, 0, bonus)`; `value + modifier` with both empty = 0; `if(true, r, 0)` deep-equals `r`; `and`/`or` with an error on either side; `if(iserror(x), 0, x)`; dot-access through a ref, on a list of refs (flattening a cell holding a list), on empty, on a deleted ref (#REF), on a roll result (`.total`, `.dice`, `.expr`, `.foo` #NAME); a dangling ref read from a cell inside a list is #REF through `FakeEnv`; bare name missing #NAME; `it` outside a predicate #NAME; arity mismatch #TYPE; unknown function #NAME; `x.where(...)` is #NAME when evaluated with `coreRegistry()` (an explicitly core-only registry, so the test stays valid after the library registers `where`); a call to a permanently unknown name (`no_such_function_zz(1)`) is #NAME with the default registry; error `origin` set from scope; parsing and evaluating a `1+1+…` chain and an `a.b.c…` chain at the parser's maximum depth gives a value (or a language error), never a stack exception; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-o9i.12); value semantics (vtt-o9i.6); the function library (vtt-o9i.7); queries (vtt-o9i.8); memoization, dependency recording, cycles (vtt-o9i.9), budgets (vtt-o9i.16).

title: Formula: rolling and roll validation
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §2.2 (rolling, roll results, keep/drop ranking, explosion and reroll rules as written by vtt-o9i.12); docs/FIXTURES.md §2 (roll result encoding), §5 (script entries are roll results to validate).

The random half of dice, on top of vtt-o9i.5's notation. Files: packages/formula/src/dice/roll.ts (and one added export line in src/dice/index.ts, which the package index already re-exports). Tests: test/dice-roll.test.ts.

- `RandomSource {int(min, max): number}` (inclusive, integers).
- `rollDice(dice, rng): RollValue`. Per term in order: roll `count` dice (1..S, or −1..1 for F). For each die in order: if a reroll condition holds, roll it once more; the new result replaces it and the original goes to `dropped` (no second reroll). Then if explode is on and the die shows S, roll an extra die, appended immediately after it; repeat while the extra shows S, at most 100 extras per original die; extras are separate dice and are not rerolled. Keep/drop then ranks all of the term's dice (including extras), ties broken by roll index ascending: `kh` and `dh` rank by value descending, `kl` and `dl` by value ascending; `kh`/`kl` keep the first N of the ranking, `dh`/`dl` drop the first N (so `dl1` drops the lowest die and `dh1` the highest). `dice` = kept dice of all terms in roll order; `dropped` = rerolled originals and keep/drop-dropped dice, in roll order; `total` = Σ sign × kept + constant; `expr` = normalized.
- `validateRoll(roll): string[]` checks a given roll result (from a fixture script or a replayed effect), per term. `expr` must parse. Terms are reconstructed in order from the flat `dice` and `dropped` lists: a term without explode or reroll contributes exactly its kept count (count, N for kh/kl, count − N for dh/dl) to `dice` and the rest of its count to `dropped`, so its boundaries are known. For every term whose boundaries are known: each kept and dropped die lies in that term's range (1..S, or −1..1 for F); counts match; keep/drop is consistent (kh: every kept ≥ every dropped of the term; kl: every kept ≤ every dropped; dh: every dropped ≥ every kept; dl: every dropped ≤ every kept). Validation proceeds term by term until the first term that explodes or rerolls; from there, boundaries are unknown, so each remaining die must lie in the union of the remaining terms' ranges, and the dropped count must be at least the remaining terms' keep/drop minimum. `total` is checked exactly whenever it is determined: always when every term has known boundaries, and also when every remaining term shares one sign (their kept dice sum with that sign). What cannot be verified, documented in the function's doc comment: which die belongs to which term, and the exact total, once exploding or rerolling pools of both signs appear together; whether an explosion or reroll actually happened.

Done when: with a scripted `RandomSource`: `4d6dl1` rolling 6,4,3,1 → `{dice:[6,4,3], dropped:[1], total:13}` (the FIXTURES §2 example); `4d6dh1` rolling 6,4,3,1 → dice [4,3,1], dropped [6]; `4d6kh3` rolling 6,4,3,1 → dice [6,4,3]; `4d6kl1` rolling 6,4,3,1 → dice [1]; ties for each of the four: `2d20kh1` rolling 7,7 keeps the first 7, `2d20kl1` rolling 7,7 keeps the first 7, `3d6dh1` rolling 5,5,2 drops the first 5, `3d6dl1` rolling 2,5,2 drops the first 2; explosion extras ranked with keep/drop for each mode (e.g. `2d6!kh1` rolling 6,3,2 ranks [6,3,2] and keeps 6; `2d6!dl1` rolling 6,1,4 drops 1); `1d6!` rolling 6,6,2 → dice [6,6,2], total 14; `1d6!` with a source that always returns 6 stops after 100 extras (101 dice); `1d20r<2` rolling 1 then 1 → dice [1], dropped [1]; `1d20-1d4` rolling 15,3 → total 12; `validateRoll` accepts every roll result in every fixture scenario's dice script and the `RollValue`s in its expectations (read with `node:fs` from packages/fixtures/scenarios/, no @vtt/fixtures import), and rejects: `{expr:"1d20", dice:[21]}`; a wrong total for `2d6+3`; `1d6+1d20` with kept `[20,1]` (per-term range); `2d6kh1` with kept `[1]`, dropped `[6]`, total 1 (keep consistency); `4d6dl1` with kept `[4,3,1]`, dropped `[6]`; a wrong kept count for `4d6dl1`; a die outside every remaining range after an exploding term; a wrong total for `1d20+1d6!` (same-sign remaining terms); and accepts an unverifiable-total case `1d6!-1d6!` while still checking ranges; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-o9i.12); notation, normalization, arithmetic, stats (vtt-o9i.5); the `roll` action step, dice sources and the dice script runner (vtt-75c.15, M5); cryptographic randomness.

Depends on: vtt-o9i.5.

title: Docs: M1 language decisions
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §2–§7 and DESIGN.md §10 (decision log) for every decision of the M1 plan, including the complete syntax contract; FIXTURES.md §4, §7, §11 and the fixtures `ErrorCodeSchema` for `#SYNTAX`.

Write every settled M1 language decision into the docs before any M1 implementation bead starts, so each implementation bead cites a doc section and none of them edits docs. This bead is the only M1 bead that touches FORMULAS.md, DESIGN.md, FIXTURES.md, or the fixture format. The parser bead (vtt-o9i.4) is explicitly authorized to run concurrently against the frozen syntax contract stated in its own text; this bead documents that same contract, and both must agree before milestone acceptance. The M2 docs bead (vtt-75c.2) runs after this one and must not rewrite these rows; decisions M2 owns (geometry module location and the geometry function contract, structural defaults, landing rules, undo, visibility, persistence, identity) are written by vtt-75c.2, not here.

Each item is an edit to the named section plus one decision-log row in DESIGN.md §10, dated 2026-11-05.

FORMULAS.md §2 (values):
1. `shape` is a value type: the value the structural `shape` cell reads as, `{type:"shape", shape}`; opaque to formulas (equality only, every other operation #TYPE; truthy); no literal syntax.
2. Value encoding: the language's values are the FIXTURES §2 tagged encoding plus the shape value and the error value `{type:"error", code, message?, origin?: {object, cell}}`; errors are never storable. Op records and the file reuse these types unchanged.
3. A ref to a deleted object read from a cell, directly or inside a list or a viewers value, makes the whole read #REF (visibility then fails closed).

FORMULAS.md §2.2 (dice and roll results):
4. Roll results outside arithmetic: they act as their total in arithmetic, comparison, numeric functions and `sum`/`avg`; render as their total in `&` and `text()`; are always truthy (a roll of total 0 is still rolled); `min`/`max`/`if`/`first`/`last` return the roll unchanged.
5. Dice dialect: lowercase `d`, uppercase `F`; each modifier kind at most once per pool, any input order; `khN`/`klN` need 1 ≤ N ≤ count, `dhN`/`dlN` need 1 ≤ N < count; count ≤ 1000, sides 2–1,000,000; no explode or reroll on `dF`; explosion extras are separate dice (not compounded), at most 100 per original die, not rerolled; reroll once, the original goes to `dropped`; keep/drop ranks all of a term's dice including extras: descending for `kh` and `dh`, ascending for `kl` and `dl`, ties by roll order; `kh`/`kl` keep the first N of that ranking and `dh`/`dl` drop the first N; `max_roll`/`min_roll` ignore explosion and rerolls; `sides` of `dF` is 3.
6. Normalized dice expression: explicit counts, modifiers in the order reroll, explode, keep/drop, integer constants folded into one trailing term, term order preserved (`1d6+1d20` ≠ `1d20+1d6`), no semantic simplification (`1d20kh1` ≠ `1d20`). Dice equality and fixture script matching use it.

FORMULAS.md §2.3 (errors):
7. `#SYNTAX`: the formula source does not parse, including exceeding the parser's limits (AST depth 256, counting every nesting including binary-operator and dot chains; 10,000 AST nodes) and a numeric literal that converts to a non-finite number.
8. Errors in lists: lists never contain errors; building a list from an error item yields that error; with several errors the first in evaluation order (left to right, list order) wins; origin is preserved through propagation.

FORMULAS.md §2 and §3 (syntax contract, complete, matching vtt-o9i.4):
9a. Whitespace (space, tab, newline) separates tokens; there are no comments. Numbers are `digits` or `digits.digits` (no exponent, no leading or trailing `.`); a number immediately followed by an identifier character is a syntax error; a numeric literal that converts to a non-finite number is a syntax error. Text is double-quoted with escapes `\"` and `\\` only; literal newlines allowed. Identifiers are `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, case-sensitive; backtick names are any non-empty text without a backtick and are always names (never keywords or dice). Dice literals follow the dialect of item 5 and win over identifiers when the following character is not an identifier character. Precedence, loosest to tightest: `or`; `and`; comparisons; `has`; `&`; `+ -`; `* / %`; prefix `-` and `not`; postfix call, dot, method; all left-associative; an unparenthesized comparison operand of a comparison is chained and evaluates to #TYPE. Records `{name: expr, …}` reject duplicate field names. A call is an identifier followed by `(`; the only methods are `.where(expr)` (exactly one argument) and `.sort(expr)` / `.sort(expr, desc)`; any other `.name(` is a syntax error. Limits as item 7.
9. Lexing and reserved words: `all` and `gm` are reserved viewer literals (`all(...)` is the aggregate call); `desc` is contextual, recognised only as `.sort(e, desc)`; `owner` in a formula is always the cell, never the symbolic `"owner"` viewer entry; `dS` is always a dice literal, so a cell named like dice needs backticks; `1d6!=3` is `1d6 != 3`.
10. Dot-access on `empty` is `empty` (a blank, not a typo).
11. Bare names inside `where`/`sort`/`objects` predicates resolve only against the item's cells (no fallback to `this`); a bare name when the item is not a ref is #TYPE; `it` works for any item.
12. `name` is literal-only in v1 (like `tag`): a formula on `name` or `tag` is refused by the store. `obj(x)`: an exact id wins; otherwise exact match over literal `name`s, which must match exactly one object (else #REF); the evaluating cell depends on the `name` cell of the object found and on the index.
13. `objects()` domain: every object in the document, including contained objects and templates.

FORMULAS.md §4 (operators):
14. `empty` in `< <= > >=` acts as 0 against numbers and roll results and as `""` against text; `empty` vs `empty` compares equal; `empty = 0` stays false.
15. Cross-kind equality: `=` never errors except on ink; different kinds are unequal (number vs roll compares the total); viewers compare as sets; `ink = x` is #TYPE unless `x` is `empty`; shapes compare structurally.
16. Numeric edge cases: IEEE doubles; `/0` and `%0` are #DIV0; any other non-finite result is #TYPE; `%` takes the sign of the dividend; `round` is half away from zero; `number()` accepts `-?digits(.digits)?` after trimming.
17. Text ordering is by Unicode code point, not UTF-16 unit.

FORMULAS.md §5 (conditionals, filtering, ordering):
18. `if` returns the chosen branch's value unchanged (a roll stays a roll).
19. Query order: results of `contents(zone)`, `zones_containing`, `on`, `objects` are ordered by ascending `z` (empty = 0), then id by code point; the evaluator sorts; "`contents`" in §5 means the function `contents(zone)`, while the `contents` cell keeps stored order. Candidates are evaluated in id code-point order before any geometry read or predicate, so which error a query returns does not depend on the host.
20. Errors in `where`/`sort`/`objects` predicates are strict: one item's error makes the whole result that error.

FORMULAS.md §6 (functions):
21. Aggregate call shape: exactly one argument; a scalar is a one-item list and `empty` is `[]` (`max(a, b)` is #TYPE: write `max([a, b])`); empty items are skipped by all aggregates except `len`; `min`/`max` return the item; `sum` of dice is #TYPE; `has` with an `empty` left side is false.
22. Spatial queries: the host supplies candidates and the evaluator computes membership, overlap and distance with the schema geometry. The candidate set is defined over literal geometry and is host-independent: every object placed directly on the board whose literal index bounds (the union of its footprint bounds and its anchor, expanded by the geometry epsilon) intersect the query bounds, plus every object on the board with any formula-valued geometry cell (`position`, `rotation`, `z`, `shape`; a cell with an override counts as literal) regardless of bounds. The host never evaluates formulas. The evaluator reads each candidate's geometry in id code-point order through ordinary (recorded) reads; an error from a geometry read, including #CYCLE, becomes the query's result; a successfully evaluated value that is not a valid position excludes the object. A spatial index is only a way of computing that set.
23. Exclusions: an object whose `position` is not two finite numbers is excluded from `contents`, `zones_containing` and `on` (not from `objects()`); a shapeless object has a point footprint, and `on()` counts a point footprint inside the other object's footprint as overlapping (the explicit exception to positive-area overlap).
24. `distance(a, b)` is Euclidean between anchors in raw board units; it is `empty` if either object is not on a board or has an invalid position, and #TYPE if they are on different boards; grid metrics and `unit` stay in §11.

FORMULAS.md §7 (evaluation model):
24a. `visible_to` is consumed through `toViewers`: the visibility code converts the evaluated `visible_to` value with `toViewers` (a viewers value as is; a ref to a character as a one-entry set; a list of refs and viewer sets as their union); anything that fails conversion (`empty`, an empty list, an error, another kind) admits nobody. So `visible_to = owner` and a list of character refs work as documented in §2.
25. Query dependencies are invalidated by changes to `position`, `rotation`, `shape`, `z`, `board`, `tag`, `container`, `is_zone`, `name`, creation, deletion (adds `name` and `is_zone`).
26. Budget (replaces any depth limit): each formula evaluation may spend 20,000 units; each cell read, each existence check, each candidate tested by a spatial query, and each id returned by `objects()`/`obj()` enumeration costs 1; reading an already computed dependency costs 1 regardless of its own cost. Because the candidate set is defined over literal geometry, the charge is the same on every host. Exceeding the budget is #LIMIT. There is no dependency-depth limit: the engine resolves dependencies iteratively, evaluates each dependency formula at most once per revision, and gives identical results across cold and warm caches and read orders.
27. Propagation is lazy pull with dirty marking: a commit marks dependents dirty once; the authority decides which cells to recompute and send.
28. The M1 fixture runner applies `set`, `override`, `clear_override`, `move`, checks `cell` and `cell_error`, and skips and reports everything else (DESIGN §10 row only).

FIXTURES.md and the fixture format: §4 replaces "once the language defines a parse-error code" with `#SYNTAX`; §7 lists `#SYNTAX` among `cell_error` codes; §11 records the additive `#SYNTAX` error code. This bead also makes the code change: add `#SYNTAX` to `ErrorCodeSchema` in packages/fixtures/src/schema.ts (the inferred type follows) and a case in packages/fixtures/test/format.test.ts accepting a `cell_error` with `#SYNTAX`. No scenario is edited. vtt-75c.2's fixture edits come after this bead.

Done when: each numbered item is present in the named section with its decision-log row dated 2026-11-05; the FIXTURES.md edits are present; `ErrorCodeSchema` accepts `#SYNTAX` and the format test covers it; no other test is required; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: any code other than the fixtures `ErrorCodeSchema` and its format test; M2's decisions (vtt-75c.2).

Depends on: none.

title: Authority: engine host adapter, recompute, visibility integration
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §3 (names, `obj()` over literal names), §3.1 (structural cells readable, defaults), §6 (the literal-geometry candidate set), §7 (revision-consistent, dynamic and query dependencies, whole-document, cycles through geometry), as written by vtt-o9i.12 and vtt-75c.2; DESIGN.md §4.2, §4.4 (cover, fail closed), §7 (formulas evaluate only in the authority; internal synchronization before notifications).

Wire the M1 engine to the document. Exclusive files: packages/authority/src/engine/host.ts, table.ts, cover.ts, index.ts (one added export line in packages/authority/src/index.ts, never reordering others). Also switches the M1 test host to the canonical structural table (below).

- host.ts, `DocumentHost`: implements vtt-o9i.3's `EvalHost` over `DocumentStore` (vtt-75c.16) and `SpatialIndex` (vtt-75c.9); it never evaluates formulas: `exists` (boards exist; a missing id is how #REF arises); `cell` (stored content with an override returned as its literal; structural cells per `STRUCTURAL_CELLS` (vtt-75c.3): `id` text, `name` literal text, `tag` list of text, `contents` list of refs, derived `container` ref or empty, `board` ref or empty, `position` list of two numbers or formula or empty, `is_zone` boolean, `shape` a `ShapeValue` or empty); `objectsNamed` (exact match over literal `name`s); `allObjects`; `objectsOnBoard(board, near)` = `index.candidates(board, near)`, exactly the literal-geometry candidate set. Exact geometry is the evaluator's (vtt-o9i.8).
- cover.ts: `opaqueZonesCovering(obj)` returns `{covering, undetermined}` as vtt-75c.10 defines: for the object's (or outermost container's) board, consider every `is_zone` candidate of `index.candidates(board, anchorBox)` and every zone on the board with formula-valued geometry, `opaque` or `is_zone`; read `is_zone`, `opaque`, `position`, `rotation`, `shape` through `engine.value`; a zone whose reads are all valid, with `opaque` true and the anchor in its region (schema `pointInRegion`, vtt-75c.7), is `covering`; a zone with any read that is an error or of the wrong type is `undetermined` (fail closed).
- table.ts, `Table`: owns a store, an index, an engine (`createEngine(host)`, vtt-o9i.9, vtt-o9i.16), and a `Visibility` (vtt-75c.10) wired with `reader.value = engine.value` and the cover query. It registers one internal commit hook (`store.onCommitInternal`, vtt-75c.16), which runs before every public `onCommit` listener, including listeners registered before the table was constructed. From the commit payload `{group, summary}` the hook applies the commit to the index and builds the M1 `Change[]` from `summary.changedCells`, `summary.created` and `summary.removed` (all derived changes included: for a move, the object's `board`, `position`, `rotation`, `z`, `container` and both containers' `contents`; for create/remove, `object_created`/`object_deleted` for every object in the subtree plus the parent's `contents`; tag and shape field changes as `cell` changes; per-cell visibility changes produce none), then calls `engine.invalidate` once. `table.value(obj, cell)` = `engine.value`. `table.isOverridden(obj, cell)`. `Table.fromSnapshot`, `Table.fromStore`.

M1 test-host switch: packages/formula/test/support/memory-host.ts (vtt-o9i.15) imports `STRUCTURAL_CELLS` / `structuralDefault` from @vtt/schema instead of its own defaults, and the @vtt/formula tests stay green unchanged.

title: Authority: serialization, load, migration
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 Persistence (the file's contents, migration, hand edits: "the snapshot wins and the operation history is kept as record, not replayed", log compaction, history invariants), with the file, barrier, asset-path and history rules written by vtt-75c.2.

Pure serialization and loading; no filesystem (that is vtt-75c.17). Exclusive files: packages/authority/src/persist/canonical.ts, serialize.ts, parse.ts, migrate.ts, compact.ts, index.ts (one added export line in packages/authority/src/index.ts, never reordering others). History is read, validated and restored only through vtt-75c.5's `History` and `validateHistory`.

- `canonicalJson(value)`: deterministic JSON, two-space indent, object keys in schema field order for known types (id first for objects), `objects`, `cells` and `cell_visibility` sorted by key, trailing newline. Same input, same bytes.
- `serializeTable(store, assets: string[])`: a `TableFile` (vtt-75c.4) with the current snapshot, `snapshot_hash = "sha256:" + hex(sha256(canonicalJson(snapshot)))`, `log = {first_index, groups, undo_barrier}` from the history, and `assets` as given; every asset path must already be relative (no leading `/`, no drive letter; else an error); the function does no path conversion.
- `parseTable(text): {store, editedExternally, warnings}` (pure): JSON parse → `migrate` from `schema_version` to `SCHEMA_VERSION` → `TableFileSchema` → `validateSnapshot` → hash check → `validateHistory(log, snapshot.revision, {editedExternally})` → a `DocumentStore` (vtt-75c.16) with the snapshot and the history restored. A newer `schema_version` than supported, a schema failure, an invariant violation, or a history violation is a load error listing every problem. If the recomputed hash differs from `snapshot_hash` (hand edit), the snapshot is used as is, the retained groups are kept as record, and the barrier is raised to the next absolute group index (`first_index + groups.length`; equal to `first_index` when the retained log is empty), so no earlier group can be undone and later groups can; `editedExternally: true`. Assets are not checked here.
- `migrate(json, migrations = MIGRATIONS)`: applies `migrations[v]` (v → v+1) in sequence; `MIGRATIONS` is empty at version 1.
- `compactLog(store, keepLast)`: delegates to `History.compact`.

Done when: tests show: `canonicalJson` byte-stable across two serializations and across parse → serialize (identical text); objects with `cell_visibility` entries on `contents` and `tag` survive serialize → parse unchanged; `serializeTable` refuses an absolute asset path; a synthetic migration registry `{1: v1→v2, 2: v2→v3}` takes a v1 file to v3 in order, and a version above the registry's is refused; a hand-edited text (one literal changed) parses with the edit, `editedExternally: true`, the log intact, earlier groups refused for undo and a newly committed group undoable; compact → serialize → hand-edit → parse with retained groups 8–9 sets the barrier to 10 (not to the retained length), blocks undo of 8 and 9, and lets a new group 10 be undone; the same with an empty retained log sets the barrier to `first_index`; load errors listing the problem for: a containment cycle, a gap in group indices, a broken revision chain, `undoes` on an edit group, an undo of an undo, a barrier beyond the next index, and a last group revision differing from the snapshot in an unedited file; compaction keeps indices and blocks undo below the kept range; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-75c.2); filesystem I/O, atomic save, asset existence, the epic acceptance test (vtt-75c.17); autosave cadence and file location (M3); importing asset files (M4); computed formula results in the file (never stored).

Depends on: vtt-75c.4, vtt-75c.8.


Decision (orchestrator, from the vtt-75c.5 review): a hand-edited file must not break the revision chain for later groups. On load, when `snapshot_hash` does not match (`editedExternally`), the loader keeps the edited snapshot's contents but sets the document revision to the last retained group's `revision` (unchanged when the retained log is empty), then raises the barrier to the next index as DESIGN §7 says. So `validateHistory` is called with `editedExternally` only for that load, and every later group chains from the last retained revision. Record this as one decision-log row in DESIGN §7 in the same commit ("revision continues from the last retained group after a hand edit").

title: Authority: visibility
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.4 (effective visibility, per-cell visibility metadata, face-down rule, opaque zones, fail closed for every evaluated input), §6 phase 1, with the cover, default, `toViewers` and fail-closed rules written by vtt-75c.2 and vtt-o9i.12; FIXTURES.md §7 (`cell_visible`, `object_visible`); FORMULAS.md §2 (viewer expressions), §9.

Exclusive file: packages/authority/src/visibility.ts (one added export line in packages/authority/src/index.ts, never reordering others). `Viewer = {type:"gm"} | {type:"character", id}`. `new Visibility(store, reader, cover)`:
- `reader.value(obj, cell)` returns the current evaluated value of a cell (the engine supplies it in vtt-75c.12; tests use a literal reader). An absent `visible_to` reads as the default viewers `all`, because the host applies structural defaults.
- `cover.opaqueZonesCovering(obj)` returns `{covering: ObjectId[], undetermined: ObjectId[]}`: zones on the object's board whose region contains its anchor and whose `opaque` is true (`covering`), and zones on that board whose `opaque`, `is_zone` or geometry could not be evaluated to valid values (`undetermined`). The engine supplies it in vtt-75c.12; tests stub it.

Rules (every evaluated input fails closed; the GM is unaffected by all of them):

- `viewerSetAdmits(value, viewer, holder)`: `value` is converted with vtt-o9i.6's `toViewers` (a viewers value as is; a ref as a one-entry set; a list of refs and viewer sets as their union); a conversion failure (`empty`, `[]`, an error, another kind) admits nobody. Within the set: `all` admits every character; a `ref` admits that character (a ref to a non-character admits nobody); `owner` admits the character in `holder`'s `owner` cell (if that cell is not a ref to a character, nobody); `gm` admits nobody but the GM.
- `isEffectivelyVisible(viewer, obj)`: `viewerSetAdmits(reader.value(obj, "visible_to"), viewer, obj)` and the container (if any) is effectively visible, recursively.
- `isCovered(viewer, obj)`: with `root` = `obj` if on a board, else its outermost container: some zone in `covering` or in `undetermined` (other than `root` itself) is not effectively visible to the viewer. Independent of `z`.
- `canSeeObject(viewer, obj)` = effectively visible and not covered (`object_visible`).
- `canSeeCell(viewer, obj, cell)`: `canSeeObject(viewer, obj)`, and the object's `cell_visibility[cell]` (store metadata; any cell name; an absent entry adds no restriction) admits the viewer with `obj` as holder, and unless `cell` is in `FACE_DOWN_EXEMPT`, the face-down rule: if `face_up` evaluates to `true` there is no restriction; if it evaluates to `false`, an error, or anything but a boolean, the viewer must be the object's `owner`. `FACE_DOWN_EXEMPT` (exported from visibility.ts) is `name`, `board`, `position`, `rotation`, `z`, `container`, `face_up`, `shape`: DESIGN §4.4, a face-down object shows its back, its placement and its name to anyone who can see the object; per-cell visibility entries still apply to these cells.
- Viewers that are not `is_character` objects see nothing.

Done when: tests with a literal reader and a stub cover show: a card `all` in a hand visible to Aldric is visible to Aldric and not to Bryn, and visible to both once its container is a board (drawing-a-card.json shape); a GM-only `ac` cell on a public goblin is hidden from Aldric while `hit` is visible (goblin-hit.json); `cell_visibility` of `gm` on `contents` and on `tag` (no such stored cells) hides those cells from Aldric while the object stays visible; a face-down card owned by Aldric shows to Bryn exactly the `FACE_DOWN_EXEMPT` cells and no other cell (a test iterates the constant against the set above), and a GM-only cell on it shows to nobody but the GM; `face_up` evaluating to an error and to a number each behave as face down; an object `all` under a hidden opaque zone is not visible to Aldric, nor is its public cell; visible once the zone is visible to all; a card in a hand under the zone is covered too; a goblin with higher `z` than the zone is still covered; a hidden zone listed as `undetermined` (opaque evaluating to an error, or geometry unreadable) covers; `visible_to` absent → visible to every character; `visible_to` evaluating to a ref to Aldric (the `visible_to = owner` shape) → visible to Aldric only; to a list of refs to Aldric and Bryn → visible to both and not to Cara; to a list mixing a ref and a viewers value → their union; to a ref to a non-character → nobody; to `empty`, `[]`, an error, and a number → hidden from every character but not the GM; `owner` in a container's `visible_to` resolves against the container's owner; a non-character viewer sees nothing; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-75c.2); evaluating formula `visible_to`, `face_up`, `opaque` and computing cover (vtt-75c.12); filtering of logs, inspector, query results by visibility (M3, M5); computed vision (Later).

Depends on: vtt-75c.16, vtt-o9i.6, vtt-75c.2.

title: Authority: spatial index (exact candidate set)
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.3 (one board per query), §7 Scale ("spatial queries are backed by an index that is invalidated on position, shape, board, tag, and deletion changes"); FORMULAS.md §6 (the literal-geometry candidate set written by vtt-o9i.12), §7 (query dependencies), with the geometry split written by vtt-75c.2.

The evaluator computes exact spatial answers (vtt-o9i.8, vtt-75c.7); this index computes, quickly, exactly the candidate set the host contract requires (vtt-o9i.3), never evaluating formulas: every object placed directly on the board whose literal `indexBounds` (vtt-75c.7: union of footprint bounds and anchor, expanded by `GEOM_EPSILON`) intersect the query bounds `near` (inclusive), plus every object on the board with any formula-valued geometry cell (`position`, `rotation`, `z`, `shape`; a cell with an override counts as literal) regardless of bounds. Not a superset and not a subset: budgets charge per candidate tested, so any difference from the reference set changes results. It never orders results and never decides membership or overlap.

Exclusive files: packages/authority/src/spatial/index.ts (and spatial/grid.ts if wanted); one added export line in packages/authority/src/index.ts, never reordering others. `SpatialIndex` is built from a `DocumentStore` (vtt-75c.16) and kept current from the commit payload (`index.applyCommit({group, summary})`, registered as an internal commit hook by vtt-75c.12): `place`, `create`, `remove`, `field` shape changes, and `cell` effects on `position`, `rotation`, `z` (including overrides set or cleared and content switching between literal and formula).

Structure: per board, a uniform grid of 8×8 board-unit buckets holding object ids by literal `indexBounds`, a per-board list for objects whose bounds span more than 64 buckets, and a per-board set of objects with formula-valued geometry, always returned. An object whose literal position is not two finite numbers (and has no formula geometry) is never a candidate.

Queries:

- `candidates(board, near: Bounds): ObjectId[]`: exactly the set defined above; unordered, each id once.
- `objectsOnBoard(board)`: every object directly on the board.

Done when: tests show: for a small board, `candidates` equals vtt-o9i.15's `literalCandidates` reference semantics re-implemented as a brute-force check in this test (every object on the board tested with `boundsIntersect(indexBounds(o), near)` over literal geometry, plus formula-geometry objects), including one exactly touching the box, one epsilon outside the box edge after expansion, a rotated rect whose rotated bounds reach it, an offset polygon (points [[10,10],[12,10],[12,12]] relative to its anchor) whose anchor lies in the box while its footprint does not, an object with a formula `position` far away (included), the same object after an override is set (included only by its override's bounds) and after the override is cleared (included again), and an object with a formula `z` (included); it never includes an object in a container or on another board; the index stays current after a move (board→board, board→container, container→board), a `position` write, a `rotation` write, a shape change, a create, a remove, and a `position` switched between literal and formula; on a generated board of 3000 objects, `candidates` for a 2×2 box returns fewer than 50 ids, and for 200 random boxes (including epsilon-boundary boxes) the result equals the brute-force set; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-75c.2); exact spatial tests, ordering and `distance` (vtt-o9i.8 with vtt-75c.7); the `EvalHost` adapter (vtt-75c.12); budget accounting (vtt-o9i.16); finer index dependency keys (Polish; the engine uses one global index key); renderer viewport culling (M4); cross-board geometry (not planned).

Depends on: vtt-75c.6, vtt-75c.7.

title: Authority: undo and replay
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 ("Undo reverses one group, and is itself an operation. Undo after an intervening operation that touched the same cells is refused with an explanation"; "Replay applies effects; it never re-rolls or re-evaluates"), with the undo targets, conflict keys, identity reservation and replay/rewind rules written by vtt-75c.2; FIXTURES.md §8 (default target, no redo, `undo_conflict`, `nothing_to_undo`, "surviving").

User undo on top of vtt-75c.5's `History`, `invertForUndo` and `touchedKeys`, and vtt-75c.16's transactions, `replay`, `rewind` and `storedStateEqual`. Exclusive file: packages/authority/src/store/undo.ts (one added export line in src/store/index.ts).

- `findUndoTarget(history, selector)`: selector `{type:"latest"}` (default; the most recent retained group that is neither an undo nor already undone), `{type:"actor", actor}` (the latest such group by that actor), or `{type:"group", index}` (absolute). Groups with index below `history.undoBarrier`, and groups no longer retained, are not candidates. No candidate → `nothing_to_undo`; an explicit index that is an undo, already undone, below the barrier, or not retained → `nothing_to_undo`.
- Conflict rule: target G conflicts with a later retained group H iff H is not an undo group, H is not undone, and `touchedKeys` of H's effects intersect G's (`obj:<id>` intersects any key on that object; create/remove include the parent's `contents` key; allocation and retirement touch nothing). Undo groups never conflict. Refusal: `undo_conflict` with `target`, `conflicting` indices, and a message naming the first conflicting group's label and the shared cell.
- `undo(store, actor, selector)`: in one transaction (`begin(actor, {kind: "undo", label, undoes: G.index})`), records `invertForUndo` of G's effects in reverse order (evaluated against the working copy); any invariant failure on commit is reported as `undo_conflict`. It appends one group; nothing is deleted; no redo. User undo never reverses `allocate` or `retire`: undoing a creation retires the created ids, undoing a removal restores the objects with their ids still retired, and `next_seq` never decreases.

Done when: tests show: the hit-points.json sequence at store level (set, override, set, clear_override, undo) ends with five groups and the override back; undo twice of two writes to the same cell restores the original; undo of a spawn removes the copies and undo of a remove restores the subtree; undo of a reorder restores order; epic criterion: actor GM writes `goblin1.damage_taken`, actor agent then writes the same cell, `undo({type:"actor", actor: gm})` is refused with `undo_conflict` naming the agent's group and changes nothing, while the same with the agent writing a different cell succeeds; undo of a move into a container is refused after a later move out of that container; undo of a spawn into a container is refused after a later reorder of that container and after a later sibling inserted into it; undo of a remove from a container is refused after a later sibling inserted into that container; identity: spawn → undo → spawn gives the second spawn new ids (the first ids stay retired, `next_seq` did not decrease); creating an object with an explicit id after undoing that id's creation is `invalid`; selective undo (`{type:"group"}`) of an older spawn while a later spawn's objects exist keeps the later objects, their ids, and `next_seq` unchanged; after undo of a spawn, the stored state equals the pre-spawn state under `storedStateEqual(…, {ignoreIdentity: true})` but not without it; board identity: adding a board, undoing that creation, then `addBoard` or `createObject` with the same id is `invalid` (the id stays retired), and spawn never generates it; `nothing_to_undo` on an empty log, after everything is undone, and for an explicit index below the barrier; `replay` of a log of mixed groups (including undos and no-effect groups) from the base reproduces `toSnapshot()` exactly, including identity bookkeeping and `revision`, and `rewind` of the head reproduces the base exactly; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-75c.2); redo (not planned); history storage, barrier and compaction (vtt-75c.5, persisted by vtt-75c.11); undo as a UI or MCP command (M3, M5).

Depends on: vtt-75c.6.


Note from vtt-75c.5 as merged: `historicalInverse(effect, stateBefore)` takes the state before the effect (the inverse of a board removal records the board's index), so inverses cannot be derived while rewinding backward from a later state. The store computes each group's historical inverses while applying or replaying forward and keeps them in memory (never persisted), or rewinds by replaying from a snapshot. `History` returns deep-frozen records (`FrozenGroup`, `DeepReadonly<TableLog>`); copy before mutating.

title: Geometry in @vtt/schema
description:
Implements: FORMULAS.md §6 (`contents(zone)`: "A point on the boundary is inside. Rotation of the zone and of the object are respected"; `on(obj)`; `distance`; the candidate set), with the coordinate, rotation, tolerance and overlap rules written by vtt-75c.2 and the candidate-set rule written by vtt-o9i.12; DESIGN.md §4.3 (anchor-point containment); FIXTURES.md §3 (Shape: rect and circle centred on the anchor, polygon points relative to the anchor; a polygon need not surround its anchor).

The one pure geometry module, in @vtt/schema so the evaluator and the authority share it: packages/schema/src/geometry/ (index.ts plus implementation files). Package index rule: add only `export * from "./geometry/index"` to packages/schema/src/index.ts; Biome requires the lines sorted, so place yours in order; never edit others' lines. No document access, no dependencies. Consumers: the formula queries (vtt-o9i.8), the spatial index (vtt-75c.9), the opaque-cover query (vtt-75c.12).

- `GEOM_EPSILON = 1e-9` (board units).
- `pointInRegion(point, shape, anchor, rotationDeg)`: boundary inclusive within `GEOM_EPSILON`, as a distance. Coordinates x right, y down; rotation degrees clockwise on screen about the anchor. Circle: `sqrt(dx²+dy²) <= r + GEOM_EPSILON` (computed with `Math.hypot`); rect and polygon: point within `GEOM_EPSILON` of any edge, else even-odd ray casting.
- `footprintsOverlap(a, b)`, each `{shape: Shape | null, anchor, rotation}`: true iff the intersection has positive area. Near-tangent shapes (touching, or penetrating by at most `GEOM_EPSILON`) do not overlap: convex pieces are separated when, on some separating axis, `max1 <= min2 + GEOM_EPSILON`; circle–circle overlaps iff `distance < r1 + r2 − GEOM_EPSILON`. Polygons are triangulated by ear clipping first (they are simple by vtt-75c.3 validation), so concave polygons are handled piecewise; circle against convex polygon uses edge normals plus the axis from the centre to the nearest vertex. Explicit exception: a point footprint (null shape) overlaps a shape iff `pointInRegion` holds (boundary inclusive); two points never overlap.
- `shapeBounds(shape | null, anchor, rotation): Bounds` (the `Bounds` type of vtt-o9i.2): the axis-aligned box of the rotated footprint; a null shape gives the degenerate box at the anchor.
- `indexBounds(shape | null, anchor, rotation): Bounds`: the union of `shapeBounds` and the anchor point, expanded by `GEOM_EPSILON` on every side. This is the box that defines the host-independent candidate set: hosts compute it from literal geometry only, and an object is a candidate for query bounds `near` iff `boundsIntersect(indexBounds(o), near)` or it has formula-valued geometry (FORMULAS §6 as written by vtt-o9i.12).
- `boundsIntersect(a, b)`: inclusive (touching boxes intersect).
- `anchorDistance(a, b)`: Euclidean between two anchors, raw board units.

Done when: table-driven tests cover: points inside, outside and on the boundary of each shape kind, including dice-tray.json (rect 4×4 at [10,0], point [12,0] inside) and the fireball.json circle (radius 4 at [10,10]: [9,10] and [12,10] inside, [16,10] and [2,10] outside, [14,10] on the boundary inside); a point at distance `r + 0.5e-9` inside and at `r + 2e-9` outside, for a tiny circle (r = 1e-6) and a huge one (r = 1e6); a rect rotated 90° and 45° with a point inside only after rotation; an L-shaped polygon with a point in its notch outside; overlap: two radius-0.5 circles at distance 1 (touching) do not overlap, at distance 0.9 overlap, at distance `1 − 0.5e-9` do not (near-tangent); tiny (r = 1e-6) and huge (r = 1e6) circle pairs just overlapping and just separated; identical rects overlap; a rect and a circle tangent do not; a rect sitting in an L-shaped polygon's notch does not overlap it while one crossing an arm does; a point footprint inside a rect and on its edge overlaps, two points never overlap; bounds of a rotated rect and of a null shape; `indexBounds` of an offset polygon (points [[10,10],[12,10],[12,12]] relative to the anchor) contains the anchor and the polygon, expanded by epsilon; `boundsIntersect` of touching boxes is true; `anchorDistance([0,0],[3,4])` = 5; @vtt/schema has no runtime dependency other than zod; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-75c.2, vtt-o9i.12); indexing and document reads (vtt-75c.9); the formula functions that apply this geometry, ordering, and the `distance` empty/#TYPE rules (vtt-o9i.8); self-intersecting polygons (rejected by vtt-75c.3); board units other than the board's own (`unit`, FORMULAS §11).

Depends on: vtt-75c.3, vtt-75c.2.

comments.author: Theodore Gast
comments.text: Codex review (.reviews/vtt-75c.7-*.md): one in-scope finding, shoelace area cancels at large coordinates; fixed before merge in 8a2d229 by measuring triangulation, placement, point tests and SAT projections relative to a shape vertex, with regression tests at 1e8 in both windings. Judgment calls accepted: exact quarter-turn rotations; round epsilon neighbourhood at rect corners; piecewise SAT with epsilon as a distance; degenerate shapes overlap nothing; ear clipping with closed-then-open retry; indexBounds widened by epsilon. Known limit: epsilon-scale behaviour is not meaningful at coordinates near 1e8.

title: Authority: move, spawn, remove primitives
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.1 (placement, containment, templates and copying, identity reservation, "Removing an object removes its contents, recursively"); FORMULAS.md §3.1 (`board`, `position`, `rotation`, `z`, `container`, `contents`, landing rule), §8.3 (`move`, `spawn`, `remove`, spawn rules); FIXTURES.md §6 (destinations, spawn `owned`). All as written by vtt-75c.2.

Structural primitives over vtt-75c.16's transactions, as functions taking the open `Transaction` first and recording effects through `tx.record`. Exclusive file: packages/authority/src/store/structural.ts (one added export line in src/store/index.ts). Uses vtt-75c.14's `writeValue` for position writes and `writeValue`/`setFormula` for initial cells.

- `move(tx, obj, dest)`, `dest` = `{type:"board", board, position}` or `{type:"container", container, index?}`. Refuses `containment_cycle` if `container` is `obj` or a descendant. Removes `obj` from its old container or board and places it (`place` effect plus cell effects). Container destination: `index` is the position after the move, default append; `index` greater than the length after removal is `invalid`; a move within the same container removes then inserts. Entering a container deletes `position`, `rotation`, `z` (recorded, so undo restores formulas). Landing on a board (including within the same board): `position` written as `writeValue` would (a formula position gets an override); `z` = 1 + the maximum literal `z` of the other objects on the target board (absent or empty as 0; formula `z` cells ignored) unless the moving object's `z` holds a formula, which is left alone; `rotation` kept on board-to-board moves and absent after leaving a container. `owner` is never touched. After a move to a board, `containerOf(obj)` is empty.
- `createObject(tx, init, dest, id?)`: a new object from partial fields, cells and `cell_visibility`; an explicit `id` must satisfy `isValidId` and not be reserved (a live object, a live board, or retired; else `invalid`); otherwise allocated. Records `create` and `allocate`; landing rules apply on a board.
- `spawn(tx, template, dest, initialCells?: Record<string, CellContent>)` returns `{root, copies: Map<ObjectId, ObjectId>}` (original → copy, for every object in the subtree; the runner's `owned` binding uses it). Copies the template and its `contents` transitively, preserving order. Ids are `<base>_<n>` with `n = next_seq`, incremented per id, skipping any reserved id (live boards included); one `allocate` effect records the ids and the `next_seq` change. Every `ref` inside a copied cell value (content, override, nested in lists, `ref` entries in viewers values) and inside copied `cell_visibility` values that names an object in the copied subtree is replaced by the copy's id; other references are kept; `cell_visibility` keys are copied as is. Formula source is copied verbatim. Each copy gets `template = ref(original)`; the root copy gets `is_template: false`; descendants keep theirs; `is_zone`, `is_character`, `tag`, `shape`, `actions` are copied. Then each `initialCells` entry replaces the root's copied content: a literal through `writeValue`, a formula (`{type:"formula", source}`) through `setFormula` (protected cells refused either way), then the root is placed at `dest` with the landing rules. A container destination without index appends. One `create` effect records the whole subtree.
- `remove(tx, obj)`: removes the object and its contents recursively; one `remove` effect stores the full subtree (preorder, including `cell_visibility`) and the root's location, and one `retire` effect adds the removed ids to `retired_ids`. References elsewhere are left dangling. The group's `names` capture the removed objects' names before removal (vtt-75c.16).

title: Authority: effects, change summary, history
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §7 (resolved effects, historical inverses vs user undo, undo conflict keys, change summary, history invariants), §4.1 (identity across boards and objects), as written by vtt-75c.2; FIXTURES.md §8.

The effect algebra, change reporting and history that the store (vtt-75c.16) and every later authority bead build on. Pure over an in-memory document state; no transactions here. Exclusive files in packages/authority/src/store/: doc.ts, effects.ts, summary.ts, history.ts, and index.ts (created here; later beads add only their own export lines and never reorder others). Add `export * from "./store/index"` to packages/authority/src/index.ts under the same rule.

- doc.ts: `DocState`, a mutable in-memory snapshot (from and to `Snapshot`) with a derived `containerOf` map and the read API the store re-exposes: `getObject`, `hasObject`, `getBoard`, `getCell` (stored `Cell` or the structural default from `STRUCTURAL_CELLS`), `getCellVisibility(obj, cell)`, `containerOf`, `boardOf`, `contentsOf`, `objectsOnBoard`, `isReserved(id)` (a live board, a live object, or retired), `nextSeq`.
- effects.ts, for every effect kind of vtt-75c.4:
  - `applyEffect(state, effect)`; `allocate` sets `next_seq` to `seq_after`; `retire` adds its ids (it records exactly the ids it adds).
  - Historical inverses: `HistoricalInverse`, an internal type (never persisted, not an `Effect`) able to express every exact reversal, including `unallocate` (restore `seq_before`) and `unretire` (remove exactly the recorded ids); `historicalInverse(effect): HistoricalInverse`; `applyHistoricalInverse(state, inv)`.
  - User undo: `invertForUndo(effect, state): Effect[]`, persisted effects: as the exact reversal for `cell`, `cell_visibility`, `field`, `place`, `reorder`; `remove` → `create` (restored ids stay retired); `create` → `remove` plus `retire` of the created ids not already retired; `board` creation (`before: null`) → board removal plus `retire` of the board id; board removal → board re-creation (id stays retired); board rename → rename back; `allocate` and `retire` → nothing (ids stay reserved, `next_seq` never decreases).
  - `touchedKeys(effect)`: `cell:<obj>/<name>` for `cell` and `cell_visibility` effects (and `cell:<obj>/<field>` for `field` effects); `cell:<container>/contents` for reorders and for both ends of a `place` into or out of a container; `cell:<obj>/board` and `cell:<obj>/position` for a `place`; for `create` and `remove`, `obj:<id>` for every object in the subtree plus `cell:<parent>/contents` when the location is a container; `board:<id>` for board effects; nothing for `allocate` and `retire`. `obj:<id>` intersects every key naming that object. Single source for undo conflicts (vtt-75c.8).
  - `changedCells(effect, stateBefore)`: every readable cell whose value the effect changes, including derived ones: a `place` changes the object's `board`, `position`, `rotation`, `z`, `container` and the `contents` of both containers; `create`/`remove` change every cell of the subtree and the parent's `contents` (container location); `field` changes the named cell; `reorder` changes `contents`; `cell_visibility` changes no readable cell.
- summary.ts: `ChangeSummary = {created: ObjectId[]; removed: ObjectId[]; boardsCreated: BoardId[]; boardsRemoved: BoardId[]; writtenCells: {object, cell, before: CellState, after: CellState}[]; visibility: {object, cell}[]; moved: {object, from: Location, to: Location, derived: CellKey[]}[]; changedCells: CellKey[]}`, built incrementally by `SummaryBuilder.add(effect, stateBefore)`. An explicit write of the same value still appears in `writtenCells`. Consumed through the store's transaction and commit payload (vtt-75c.16) by the engine adapter (vtt-75c.12) and the action context (vtt-75c.15).
- history.ts: `History`, the only owner of the log: absolute group indices; `firstIndex`, `nextIndex` (`firstIndex + retained count`), `undoBarrier` (absolute; never lowered except by `restore`), `groups()`, `get(index)`, `isUndone(index)`, `append(group)` (assigns `index = nextIndex`), `restore({first_index, groups, undo_barrier}, snapshotRevision, {editedExternally})`, `compact(keepLast)` (keeps the last `keepLast` groups with their indices, advances `firstIndex`, raises the barrier to at least `firstIndex`; `keepLast = 0` leaves an empty log with `firstIndex = nextIndex`), `raiseBarrier(index)`. `validateHistory(log, snapshotRevision, {editedExternally})` returns every violation of the invariants in DESIGN §7: contiguous indices from `first_index`; `revision = base_revision + 1` and each `base_revision` equal to the previous group's `revision`; `kind: "undo"` iff `undoes` present; `undoes` is an earlier index that is not an undo group (or below `first_index`), and no index undone twice; barrier within `first_index … nextIndex`; last retained `revision` equals the snapshot's unless `editedExternally`. `restore` refuses a log with violations.

Done when: tests (test/store/effects.test.ts, summary.test.ts, history.test.ts) show: `applyHistoricalInverse(historicalInverse(e))` after `applyEffect(e)` restores the state exactly (including `next_seq` and `retired_ids`) for one example of every effect kind; `retire` applied to ids some of which are already retired records only the new ones and its historical inverse removes only those; `invertForUndo` of a `create` removes and retires, of a board creation removes the board and retires its id, of `allocate`/`retire` is empty; `touchedKeys` of a `create` into a container and a `remove` from one include the parent's `contents` key; `changedCells` of a container-to-board `place` lists the object's `board`, `position`, `z`, `container` and the old container's `contents`; a summary over a transaction-like sequence (spawn into a container, write the same value twice, move, remove) lists created, written (including the same-value write), moved with derived keys, and removed objects; `History` compaction (groups 0–9, `compact(2)` → indices 8, 9, `firstIndex` 8, barrier ≥ 8; `compact(0)` → empty, `firstIndex = nextIndex = 10`); `validateHistory` reports each violation (a gap in indices, a broken revision chain, `undoes` on a non-undo group, an undo of an undo, a double undo, a barrier out of range, a final revision differing from the snapshot) and accepts the last one when `editedExternally`; `restore` refuses an invalid log and reproduces indices and barrier for a valid one; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-75c.2); the store, transactions, replay and comparison (vtt-75c.16); edit and structural primitives (vtt-75c.14, vtt-75c.6); undo selection (vtt-75c.8); persistence (vtt-75c.11).

title: Schema: document, objects, structural cells, validation
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.1 (objects, identity reservation), §4.3 (zones and boards), §4.4 (stored `visible_to` and per-cell visibility metadata), §7 (canonical schema); FORMULAS.md §3, §3.1 (defaults, literal-only `name` and `tag`, edit-only `shape`); FIXTURES.md §3. All as written by vtt-75c.2 and vtt-o9i.12.

Build the canonical document types in @vtt/schema with zod schemas and an invariant checker, on top of vtt-o9i.2's value, id, shape and cell-content types (not redefined). Adds `zod` 4.6.7 (the version @vtt/fixtures uses) to @vtt/schema.

Files in packages/schema/src/; tests in test/ per file. Package index rule: add only this bead's `export * from "./<module>"` lines to src/index.ts; Biome requires the lines sorted, so place yours in order; never edit other beads' lines.

- ids.ts (exists from vtt-o9i.2): add `BoardId`, `RESERVED_IDS` (`gm`, `all`, `owner`), `isValidId` (matches the existing `ID_PATTERN` and is not reserved).
- shape.ts (exists): add `ShapeSchema`.
- cell.ts (exists): add `Cell = {content: CellContent; override?: Value}` and `CellSchema`; `ValueSchema` and `CellContentSchema` are zod wrappers delegating to `isValue` / `isCellContent`.
- structural.ts: `STRUCTURAL_CELLS`, `StructuralCellSpec`, `structuralDefault(name, obj)`.
- object.ts: `TableObject`, `ActionDef` (`{name, when?, steps: string[]}`, source text), schemas.
- document.ts: `Board = {id: BoardId; name?: string}` (as the fixtures `BoardSchema`), `Snapshot`, `SnapshotSchema`.
- validate.ts: `validateSnapshot(s): Violation[]`.

```ts
type TableObject = {
  id: ObjectId;
  is_template: boolean; is_zone: boolean; is_character: boolean;
  tag: string[];                                   // literal list of text
  shape: Shape | null;                             // relative to the anchor
  board: BoardId | null;                           // non-null iff on a board
  contents: ObjectId[];                            // owning, ordered
  cells: Record<string, Cell>;                     // ordinary cells plus name, visible_to, owner,
                                                   // template, face_up, opaque, position, rotation, z
  cell_visibility: Record<string, ViewersValue>;   // per-cell visibility, independent of content
  actions: ActionDef[];
};
type Snapshot = { revision: number; next_seq: number; boards: Board[];
                  objects: Record<ObjectId, TableObject>; retired_ids: ObjectId[] };
```

`position` is a cell (a list of two numbers, or a formula, with override support), present iff `board` is non-null; `rotation` and `z` are absent for objects in containers. `container` is never stored. `cells` and `cell_visibility` use null-prototype records or are validated so `__proto__` is rejected as a key (FIXTURES §1); any other non-empty string is a valid cell name.

`cell_visibility` is the canonical per-cell visibility (DESIGN §4.4): a key may name any user cell or any FORMULAS §3.1 structural cell, whether stored as a cell, stored as a field (`tag`, `contents`, `shape`, `is_zone`, …), derived (`container`), or currently absent; the value is a literal viewers value (non-empty; refs inside may dangle). A cell with no entry defaults to its object's visibility. It maps one to one onto the fixture `cell_visibility`.

Ids form one namespace across boards and objects. `retired_ids` is the monotonic set of board and object ids that were removed at some point (by removal or by undoing a creation); together with live ids and `next_seq` it makes every id reserved for the document's lifetime. A live object's or board's id may appear in `retired_ids` (restored by undo); an id is available for a new board or object iff it is neither live (as either) nor retired. `isReserved(snapshot, id)` is exported for the store.

`STRUCTURAL_CELLS` is the canonical table, one entry per FORMULAS §3.1 cell: storage (field or cell), protection (`full` for `id`, `board`, `is_zone`; `membership` for `contents`; `derived` for `container`; `edit_only` for `shape`, which no cell write or action may change and only `setShape` changes; none otherwise), literal type, whether a formula is allowed (all cells except `template`, `tag` and `name`; fields never), how it reads (`shape` as a `ShapeValue`, or empty), and the default when absent:

| Cell | Default |
|---|---|
| name | empty |
| tag | [] |
| visible_to | viewers ["all"] |
| owner, template | empty |
| contents | [] |
| container | empty |
| board, position | empty (in a container) |
| rotation, z | empty (read as 0 by geometry and ordering) |
| face_up | true |
| opaque | false |
| is_zone | false |
| shape | empty (no shape) |

The M1 test host (vtt-o9i.3) carries a copy of this table; vtt-75c.12 switches it to import this one.

`validateSnapshot` returns every violation: ids satisfy `isValidId` and are unique across boards and objects; every key of `objects` equals that object's `id`; `cells` never stores a field-backed or derived structural name (`id`, `tag`, `contents`, `container`, `board`, `shape`, `is_zone`) nor the field names `is_template` and `is_character`; an `override` is present only when `content` is a formula, and an override on a structural cell type-checks like a literal of that cell (e.g. a `position` override is a list of two finite numbers, a `visible_to` override a viewers value); every object is on exactly one board or in exactly one `contents`; containment is acyclic; `contents` and `board` name existing objects and boards; `position` present iff on a board, `position`/`rotation`/`z` absent in a container; literal structural cells type-check (`name` text; `visible_to` viewers; `owner`, `template` ref or empty; `face_up`, `opaque` boolean; `rotation`, `z` number or empty; `position` list of two finite numbers); `opaque` only on `is_zone` objects; `template`, `name` never formulas; every `cell_visibility` value a non-empty viewers value; shapes valid (circle radius > 0, rect width and height > 0, polygon at least three points and simple); `next_seq` a non-negative integer; every `retired_ids` entry a valid id, no duplicates. References inside values may dangle; they are not violations.

Done when: for each violation kind a test builds a minimal snapshot that triggers it and asserts it is reported (and a valid snapshot reports none), including a formula `name`, a formula `template`, an empty viewers value in `cell_visibility`, a duplicate retired id, an object-map key differing from the object's id, a board and an object sharing an id, a stored cell named each of `id`, `tag`, `contents`, `container`, `board`, `shape`, `is_zone`, `is_template`, `is_character`, an override on a literal cell, a `position` override that is not two finite numbers, and a `face_up` override that is not a boolean; a live object and a live board whose ids are in `retired_ids` validate; `isReserved` is true for a live board id, a live object id and a retired id; zod schemas reject unknown keys and a `__proto__` key in `cells` and `cell_visibility`; a snapshot equivalent to the `setup` of fireball.json (written by hand) validates; a snapshot whose objects carry `cell_visibility` entries for `contents` and `tag` (no such cells stored) round-trips through `JSON.stringify` → `SnapshotSchema.parse` deep-equal; a test iterates `STRUCTURAL_CELLS` against the default table above; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test` exit 0.

Out of scope: docs (vtt-75c.2); operation records and file envelope (vtt-75c.4); conversion from fixtures (vtt-75c.13); geometry beyond shape validity (vtt-75c.7); face layout (M5); redefining value types (vtt-o9i.2).

title: Docs: M2 decisions and replay expectation
description:
Implements: DESIGN.md §4.1, §4.3, §4.4, §7 and §10 (decision log); FORMULAS.md §3.1, §6, §8.3; FIXTURES.md §3, §5, §6, §7, §8, §11. Planning bead vtt-75c.1 comments 1 and 2; the orchestrator's decisions on the M1 and M2 plans and on Codex's M2 review.

Write down every semantic decision the M2 beads implement, so each later bead cites a doc section instead of the plan. This is the only M2 bead that edits DESIGN.md, FORMULAS.md or FIXTURES.md. It runs after the M1 docs bead (vtt-o9i.12), which owns the M1 language rows (values, dice, errors, names including literal-only `name`, operators, query order and candidate set, `distance`, budgets, propagation); this bead must not write or rewrite those rows, and refers to them where it touches the same sections. Docs-only except for the additive fixture format change at the end.

Each item is an edit to the named section plus one decision-log row in DESIGN.md §10, dated 2026-11-05.

DESIGN.md §4.1 (objects):
1. `move` never changes the `owner` cell; "moving onto a board ends ownership" becomes "ends containment".
2. `is_character`: a per-object field like `is_template` (not a FORMULAS §3.1 cell), copied on spawn; view-as lists objects with `is_character` true and `is_template` false; a viewer that is not a character sees nothing; `owner` is not validated against it. Fixture runners (the M1 test host and the M2 runner) set it for ids in `setup.characters`.
3. Spawn (also FORMULAS §8.3): generated ids `<original id>_<n>` from the document counter `next_seq`, skipping any reserved id; every copy's `template` refers to its original; the root copy has `is_template: false`, descendants keep theirs; `is_zone`, `is_character`, `tag`, `shape`, `actions` and per-cell visibility are copied; refs inside copied cell values and per-cell visibility that name an object in the copied subtree are remapped to the copy, others kept; formula source is copied verbatim; a container destination without index appends, so successive spawns in one transaction append in call order.
4. Identity: an id is reserved for the document's lifetime once allocated, across boards and objects together (one namespace). `next_seq` only increases and `retired_ids` only grows; user undo never decreases the one or shrinks the other. Creating a board allocates its id; undoing a board's creation removes it and retires the id. Undoing an object's creation removes the objects and retires their ids; undoing a removal restores the objects under their own ids (which stay in `retired_ids`, so allocation never hands them out again). Only historical rewind (replaying or rewinding recorded effects from a snapshot) resets these counters.
5. Removing an object removes its contents recursively; references elsewhere dangle and evaluate to #REF; undo restores the subtree.

FORMULAS.md §3.1 (structural cells):
6. Default column: `name` empty; `tag` `[]`; `visible_to` viewers `all`; `owner`, `template` empty; `contents` `[]`; `container` empty; `board`, `position` empty in a container; `rotation`, `z` empty (read as 0 by geometry and ordering); `face_up` true; `opaque` false; `is_zone` false; `shape` empty. `is_template` and `is_character` are object fields, false by default.
7. `position` is a list of two numbers `[x, y]`, present iff the object is on a board; board units, x right, y down; `rotation` is degrees clockwise on screen about the anchor; empty `rotation` and `z` read as 0.
8. Landing rule: every `move` or `spawn` onto a board (including within the same board) puts the object on top: `z` = 1 + the maximum literal `z` of the other objects on that board (absent or empty as 0), unless the object's `z` holds a formula, which is left alone; `position` is written as a hand edit (a formula position gets an override); `rotation` is kept on board-to-board moves; entering a container deletes `position`, `rotation`, `z` (recorded, so undo restores formulas); after a move to a board `container` is empty.
9. `tag` is literal only; `set(tag, list)` is allowed. `shape` cannot be written by actions or cell writes (`set` on `shape` is refused); it changes only through the `setShape` edit primitive used by the UI and agent (its formula-side value is vtt-o9i.12's row). `template` is set on every spawned copy and is never a formula. (`name` literal-only is vtt-o9i.12's row.)

FORMULAS.md §6 (spatial functions) and DESIGN.md §4.3:
10. Exact spatial semantics live in one pure module, `packages/schema/src/geometry/`. The host returns the literal-geometry candidate set defined in vtt-o9i.12's §6 row (it never evaluates formulas); the authority's spatial index is how the authority computes exactly that set; the evaluator computes membership, overlap and distance; the opaque-cover test uses the same geometry.
11. Geometry tolerance: point membership is boundary inclusive within 1e-9 board units for every shape; for circles the test is distance-based, `sqrt(dx²+dy²) <= r + 1e-9`.
12. Overlap: two footprints overlap iff their intersection has positive area; shapes that touch or penetrate by at most 1e-9 (near-tangent) do not overlap. Explicit exception: a point footprint (shapeless object) overlaps a shape iff the point is in the shape's region (boundary inclusive); two points never overlap. Zones are never in `on()` results. Polygons must be simple.

DESIGN.md §4.4 (visibility):
13. Opaque cover is independent of `z`: an object is covered for a viewer iff it is on the same board as an opaque zone the viewer cannot effectively see and its anchor lies in the zone's region; an object inside a container is covered iff its outermost container is; a zone never covers itself; the renderer still draws the cover above everything.
14. A cell is visible to a viewer only if its object is (`object_visible`, which includes cover); then the cell's own visibility and the face-down rule apply.
15. `visible_to`: an absent cell reads as the default `all`; a present cell's evaluated value is converted with `toViewers` as vtt-o9i.12's row states (so `visible_to = owner` and lists of character refs work), and a value that fails conversion admits nobody. The `owner` viewer entry resolves against the object that holds the viewer set.
15a. Every evaluated visibility input fails closed: a `face_up` that is an error or not a boolean is treated as face down; an `opaque` that is an error or not a boolean is treated as opaque; a zone whose geometry (board, position, rotation, shape) cannot be read or is invalid, and which the viewer cannot see, is treated as covering every object on its board. The GM is unaffected.
16. Per-cell visibility is per-object metadata, `cell_visibility: {cellName: viewers}`, independent of cell content: valid for any user or structural cell name, including cells that are absent or field-backed (`tag`, `contents`, `position`, …); values are literal viewer sets; a cell with no entry defaults to its object's visibility.

DESIGN.md §7 (document, operations, persistence):
17. The operation record: a group holds resolved effects (cell before/after states with cause edit or roll; per-cell visibility changes; field changes; placements; create and remove of whole subtrees; reorders; board changes; id allocation; id retirement), the actor, kind (edit, action, undo), label, origin, `undoes`, `base_revision`, `revision`, and the names of touched objects captured at commit time (for a removed object, its name just before removal). A logged write records the resulting value (`add` logs the sum).
18. Transactions: one transaction is open at a time; the commit point is the moment the new document and the appended group are published; internal synchronization (formula invalidation, index update) runs right after it and before any public commit notification; a listener error is reported separately and never turns a commit into an abort. Before the commit point, a refusal (`Rejected`) becomes a rejection result, and any other error aborts the transaction and propagates unchanged; in both cases no dice entries or randomness are consumed. Every commit carries a change summary (created and removed objects, written cells with before/after, moved objects with derived changes).
19. Undo targets: `latest` (the most recent group that is neither an undo nor already undone; the fixture `undo` step always means this), `actor` (the latest such group by a given actor), `group` (an explicit absolute index). No redo. Undo adds its own group.
20. Undo conflict: target G conflicts with a later group H iff H is not an undo group, H is not undone, and they share a touched key: cell keys; per-cell visibility changes touch the cell's key; the `contents` key of the container at both ends of a move; creating or removing objects touches every key on those objects and the `contents` key of the container they were created in or removed from. Allocation and retirement touch nothing. Undo groups never conflict. An undo whose inverse fails an invariant on commit is refused as `undo_conflict`. This defines "surviving" in FIXTURES §8.
21. Replay and rewind: replaying a group applies its recorded effects and sets `revision` to the group's `revision` (also for groups with no effects); rewinding applies exact historical inverses (an internal representation, never persisted, distinct from user-undo effects; a retirement records exactly the ids it added, so rewind removes exactly those) and sets `revision` to the group's `base_revision`. Comparisons of stored state for replay exclude `revision`.
21a. History invariants (checked on load): retained groups have contiguous absolute indices starting at `first_index`; each group's `revision` is its `base_revision + 1` and each `base_revision` equals the previous group's `revision`; `kind: "undo"` iff `undoes` is present; `undoes` names an earlier index that is not itself an undo group (or an index below `first_index`, compacted away) and no index is undone twice; `undo_barrier` lies in `first_index … next index`; the last retained group's `revision` equals the snapshot's, except when the file was edited by hand (the barrier then equals the next index and the snapshot wins).
22. The file holds a fresh snapshot at every save plus the retained groups as history (absolute group indices, `first_index`, `undo_barrier`); there are no operations "since" the snapshot. A `snapshot_hash` detects hand edits; after one, the snapshot wins and the undo barrier is set to the next absolute group index, so every earlier group stays as record and new groups remain undoable; with an empty retained log the next index is `first_index`. Snapshots are taken at every save and at load (in-memory checkpoints are Polish; autosave cadence is M3). An older `schema_version` migrates step by step. Compaction drops old groups, keeps absolute indices, and raises the barrier to at least `first_index`.
